items.reason: Pressing D2/D3/D4 sets selectedItem to 1/2/3 and resets displayPhase; the display value alternates between selectedItem (phase<1000) and the price (phase>=1000), so both item number and price are shown on the TM1637.

On D7 release (previousConfirm true, io_3 false, not handled, not admin, selectedItem>0) with stock>0, saleItem is set, stock decremented, beepFrequency=2000/beepRemaining=100, and loop prints dispense:itemX for the matching saleItem.
When selected stock is 0, the else branch sets displayError=true (display shows -1 via conditional_42=-1) and beeps at 1000Hz for 500ms, satisfying alarm plus error code display.
While D7 held (previousConfirm true, not handled), holdDuration accumulates elapsed ms; at >=2000 adminMode toggles true and holdHandled set, entering admin mode on long press.
In admin mode, a valid RESTOCKn payload (10000..39999) updates the corresponding stock variable (stockOne/Two/Three) with clamping to 9999.

setup() calls Serial.begin(9600), constructs TM1637Display with CLK=4/DIO=5, sets pinMode for A1 input, D2 input pullup, D10 output, D6 output, D13 output, and loop reads analogRead(A1). All required initializations present.
temperature = io_0*500/1023 (LM35 10mV/°C). cooling set true at >=8, false at <=6, hysteresis. io_2=cooling drives digitalWrite(10). Relay controlled by temperature.

duration computed from opened timestamp while door open; alarm=duration>10000. io_3=1000 (tone) when alarm, io_5 toggles every 500ms within each second (blink). D6 tone and D13 LED driven accordingly.
critical=io_1 && temperature>8. serial trigger fires on rising critical or every 1000ms while critical persists, printing 'critical cooling loss: '. Continuous output while temp>8 and door open.
io_4 alternates every 2s between temperature and door-open seconds (duration/1000 capped 9999). Display shows io_4 via showNumberDec. Both temperature and door-open duration are displayed.
setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init, Serial.begin(9600), pinMode for D2, D3, A0, D6, D13, and constructs TM1637Display with CLK=4, DIO=5. All required devices are initialized.
night = selection==0 && io_2<300; armed = selection==1 || night. With selection default 0 and A0 reading below 300, armed becomes true automatically, entering night armed mode.

alarm = armed && io_0 && io_1 (PIR and door both HIGH). On rising edge count increments (capped 9999), buzzer toggles via io_3, LED via io_4, and count is shown on TM1637 via io_5. All required outputs occur.
hw_rx_parse maps "ARM" to value 1; ProgramPage1 sets selection=1 when io_6_valid && io_6==1, making armed true.
"DISARM" maps to value 2; ProgramPage1 sets selection=2, so night=false and armed=false (selection!=1), entering disarmed mode.
"STATUS" maps to value 4; ProgramPage1 prints mode (NIGHT/ARMED/DISARMED) and events count over Serial.
"RESET" maps to value 3; ProgramPage1 sets count=0 and selection=0, clearing event count and returning to auto/night mode.

setup() configures pin 12/13 outputs, pin 6 output with tone, TM1637 on (4,5), pin 8 output (vehicle Trig), pin 9 input (vehicle Echo), pin 10 output (ped Trig), pin 11 input (ped Echo). All required pins initialized to usable state.
When risk true, io_4=risk && now%1000<500 toggles red LED (blink), io_6=1000 drives tone(6,1000) buzzer, io_7=level (1 or 2) shown on TM1637. All three outputs active during danger.
When not risk, io_5=!risk is true, and loop writes digitalWrite(13, HIGH) making green LED on. No other code turns it off while safe.
On falling edge of risk (serial_0_trigger=!risk && previous), value = now-entered where entered=firstOverlap at risk onset, giving duration of last danger event; printed via Serial.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init, Serial.begin(9600), pinMode for D2/D3/D7 inputs, TM1637 brightness on D4/D5, pinMode(6,OUTPUT) for buzzer, pinMode(13,OUTPUT) for LED, and loop() runs ProgramPage1 each cycle, entering the counting state.
count sums the three sampled occupancy booleans from D2/D3/D7 and is written to io_3 each loop iteration.
hw_value_io_3 (the count) is shown via showNumberDec on the TM1637 whenever it changes, including the initial setup write.
When a layer is vacant and not yet reported and now-vacantSince exceeds 60000 ms, io_8 is set true; loop prints "restock needed" when hw_value_io_8 is true.

On transition to full, beeping is set true and tone(6,1000) is issued; recordsLocked is declared but never set or used, so no locking of new records is implemented. The buzzer part works but the lock obligation is absent.
QUERY parses to io_7==1, sets serial_0_trigger, and loop prints level1/2/3_occupied with the sampled booleans.
RESET parses to io_7==2, sets reset true, and the loop resets vacantSince and reported for all layers, restarting the vacancy timers.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init, Serial.begin, pinModes for buttons/A0/buzzer/LED, sets brightness, and shows hw_value_io_6 (initialized 0) on the TM1637. However the display shows only the floor value (io_6 = currentFloor), not the load percentage, and the initial display shows 0 rather than floor 1. The required initial display of current floor and load percentage is not implemented.

When loadPercent > 80, io_4=1000 (tone on D6) and io_5=true (LED D13). But the button-press block at lines 94-115 runs before the load check and unconditionally sets pendingMove=true, targetFloor, and moveRemainingMs=1000 regardless of load. So an over-limit press still starts a move; floor change is not prevented.

Button press sets pendingMove and moveRemainingMs=1000, but moveRemainingMs is never decremented anywhere in loop or ProgramPage1, so it stays 1000 > 0 forever; currentFloor never updates to targetFloor and movementCompletePulse never becomes true, so no "movement complete" is printed. The delay simulation and completion output are not implemented.

loadPercent is never computed from A0; hw_value_io_3 (raw analogRead) is passed as io_3 but ProgramPage1 never uses io_3, and sysml_state_loadPercent stays 0. The display shows only currentFloor (io_6), never a load percentage.
setup() configures A0/A1/A2 as INPUT, D10/D13/D6 as OUTPUT, constructs TM1637Display on pins 4/5, and sets D2 as INPUT_PULLUP; all required devices are initialized.

In auto mode (automatic=true), pump = water && io_0<512 && io_1>=512. With soil dry (io_0<512), no rain (io_1>=512), water sufficient (io_2>=512), pump is true and digitalWrite(10,HIGH) drives the relay.
If any of the three conditions fails, the corresponding conjunct is false, so pump is false and D10 is written LOW; no other path sets io_3 true in auto mode.
When water is insufficient (io_2<512), water=false forces pump=false so D10 stays LOW, and io_4=pump||!water=true drives D13 HIGH and io_5=1000 triggers tone(6,1000) on D6, providing alarm.
Button press edge (io_7 && !previous) toggles automatic from true to false; debounced input on D2 feeds io_7, so pressing the button switches auto/manual mode.
In manual mode (automatic=false), a second press with !forced sets forced=true and began=millis(); pump=water&&forced drives D10 HIGH, and forced clears after 5000ms, giving a 5-second forced run.
page=millis()/2000%3 cycles 0,1,2; io_6 outputs soil moisture (io_0), water level (io_2), and mode (0 auto/1 manual), and the display is updated when the value changes.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init, Serial.begin, TM1637 brightness on pins 4/5, pinMode for D2/D3/D7 as INPUT_PULLUP, D6 OUTPUT, D13 OUTPUT, and initializes display/tone/LED. ProgramPage1 static state has selected=0, stage=0, duration[3]={2000,2000,2000}, active=false, so it enters a settable three-stage countdown configuration state.
When not active, a rising edge on io_1 (D2) adds 1000 to duration[selected] up to 9999000. The display output uses duration[selected] when inactive, so the increase is observable.
When not active, a rising edge on io_2 (D3) advances selected=(selected+1)%3, cycling through the three stages. The display then shows duration[selected].
A rising edge on io_3 (D7) when !active resets measured[], stage=0, complete=false, and sets active=running=true, starting the countdown.
When active and io_3 rising edge occurs, running=!running toggles pause/resume. While running is false, measured[] is not incremented, so the countdown pauses.

On stage completion, pulses=stage+1 (1,2,3 beeps), beganBeep=now, and stage increments; if stage reaches 3, active/running stop and complete=true. The buzzer output toggles 1000Hz for 150ms per 300ms period for pulses count, then pulses=0. Stage auto-advances via ++stage.
When all three stages complete, complete=true is set. io_5=complete drives digitalWrite(13, HIGH) in loop, so D13 stays HIGH (LED on) after completion.

On completion report=true triggers Serial.println("process complete") in ProgramPage1, and loop prints stage1/2/3_elapsed_ms from measured[] values. measured[] accumulates elapsed per stage while running.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init (alertLevel=0), Serial.begin(9600), pinMode for A1, A0, D2, D6, D13, D12, and TM1637Display constructed with CLK=4,DIO=5 with setBrightness. All required peripherals initialized and state reset to normal level 0.

level computed as io_2 || (hot&&smoky) ? 2 : (hot||smoky ? 1 : 0). When exactly one of hot/smoky is true and no flame, level=1 (关注). hot=temperature>=50, smoky=io_1>=550. So a single mild exceed yields level 1.
level=2 when io_2 (flame) true OR both hot and smoky true. This matches multiple indicators exceeding or flame triggering.

io_3 = alarm && now%1000<500 ? 1000 : 0. In alarm, tone toggles 1000Hz for 500ms then off for 500ms repeatedly — continuous intermittent alarm. Wrapper calls tone(6,...) when value in [31,65535] and noTone when 0.
ProgramPage1 prints Serial.println("fire alert") when serial_0_trigger true, which is alarm && (!previous || now-last>=1000). In alarm this fires at least once per second.
io_6 cycles every 2s among level, temperature, smoke value; wrapper shows it on TM1637 via showNumberDec. So display shows level number and key values.
automaticMode initialized true; mode button D2 press event toggles it (line 233), and the control block branches on automaticMode (263) vs manual (284), so both modes exist and are switchable.
In auto mode fanCommand is computed from savedTemperature: 0 if <=25, 255 if >=35, else linear (T-25)*255/10; written to D5 via analogWrite. Temperature comes from DHT11 on D7.
Auto mode sets lightCommand = (io_2 < 400.0) where io_2 is analogRead(A0); D9 driven from lightCommand.
Auto mode sets pumpCommand = (io_3 < 400.0) with io_3 from analogRead(A1); D10 driven from pumpCommand.
Select button D3 press event in manual mode cycles selectedActuator 0->1->2->0.
Manual mode maps A2 (io_4) to the selected actuator: fan PWM scaled, light/pump thresholded at 512.
displayPhase cycles 0-6000ms; value_7 selects temperature (<2000), light (<4000), soil (else), written to TM1637.
io_11 = 2000 when operational and any fault (value_11) present; tone(6,2000) drives D6 buzzer.
serial_0_trigger = reportEvent (fault transition); loop prints fault messages for DHT, light, soil when triggered.

Loop scans buttons in order and only assigns playerId when sysml_state_playerId==0, breaking after the first detected press; subsequent presses are ignored because the else-if guard requires playerId==0. First press wins.
playerId is written to io_7 and the loop displays hw_value_io_7 via showNumberDec when it changes; after a press playerId becomes 1-4 and is shown on TM1637.
On a press beeping=true and winTime=now; io_6 becomes 1000 while beeping, driving tone(6,1000); after 200ms beeping clears and io_6=0 calls noTone. Short beep confirmed.
After a press playerId!=0, so the else-if branch requiring playerId==0 is skipped; no further button can set playerId until reset sets playerId=0. Other inputs locked.
On press serial_0_trigger=true and winTime/playerId are output; loop prints timestamp_ms and player_id values. Timestamp is winTime (millis at press).
When io_4 (D9) is pressed, on the rising edge of resetHeld, playerId is set to 0, clearing the lock; subsequent presses can be recorded again. Reset releases lock.
While io_4 held, after 3000ms since resetStart, wins[] is zeroed and clearDone set; this clears cumulative win statistics. Long press 3s clears stats.

On a rising edge of D2/D3/D4 (io_0/io_1/io_2 with !previousIo), callActive is set true, highestBedId and oldestWaitingBedId are set, and ageOfOldestMs is reset to 0. callActive drives io_4 which sets D13 HIGH and io_5=1000 which calls tone(6,1000), so an alarm is triggered. However, the 'waiting time' is never accumulated: ageOfOldestMs is only ever set to 0 or copied, never incremented by elapsed time, so the recorded waiting time is always 0. The order is partially captured via highestBedId but the waiting-time recording obligation is not implemented.

When D7 (io_3) is HIGH and callActive is true, the block clears callActive, highestBedId, oldestWaitingBedId, ageOfOldestMs and sets serialPending=true. serialPending drives serial_0_trigger, and loop prints wait_time_ms and bed_id via Serial. But the log values are read after the clear: serial_0_value_0 = ageOfOldestMs (now 0) and serial_0_value_1 = highestBedId (now 0), so the log always outputs 0/0 rather than the cleared call's bed and wait time. The clear happens but the processing log content is wrong.

io_6 (display value) is set to oldestWaitingBedId when callActive, else 0, and shown via showNumberDec. But oldestWaitingBedId is only ever set to a bed id (1/2/3) or 0; the seconds (ageOfOldestMs) are never displayed and never incremented, so the display shows only the bed number with no seconds. The 'bed number and seconds' obligation is not met.
ProgramPage1_Init sets sysml_state_stage=1 and setup calls it, so the initial stage is 1 (preheat).

Only io_1 (D2) is used, and only to set running=true. io_2 (D3) and io_3 (D4) are passed but never read; no code changes targetTempC or remainingMs from buttons. D4 is also configured as INPUT while TM1637 CLK is D7, so D4 is unused.
When running and io_0 >= targetTempC, beepActive=true, which yields io_4=1000, and loop calls tone(6,1000). So the buzzer sounds on reaching target.

remainingMs is never decremented (line 80 is a self-assignment), so it stays 0 after start; the <=0 branch fires every loop, advancing stage 1->2->3 and then staying at 3, never returning. Stage transition occurs but not driven by duration end; also stage 3 loops to 3. The duration-end trigger is not implemented.
io_6 is set to sysml_state_stage only, and the display shows that number. Remaining time is never output to the display; only stage number is shown.

Serial prints only three fields (elapsed_delta_ms always 0, stage_id, measured temperature) and only while running. No stage transitions, target temps, or remaining time are logged, so the full flow log is not produced.

setup() initializes A0/A1 as inputs, D2/D3 as INPUT_PULLUP, D10 as output, attaches servo on D9, and constructs TM1637Display with CLK=4, DIO=5; loop() runs the model and drives outputs, so all devices are initialized and the system enters operation.

In auto mode, when io_1 (A1 raw ADC) < 30.0 and io_0 (A0 raw ADC) > 400.0, curAnglePercent=0 and lightMode=false; loop writes servo to 0 and LED LOW. However the temperature threshold compares raw ADC counts to 30.0, which is essentially always true (ADC 0-1023), so the light-too-strong branch is unreachable in practice: io_1>=30.0 forces curtain closed regardless. The 'light too strong' condition path exists but is shadowed by the temperature branch due to unit mismatch.

When io_0 <= 400.0 (and io_1 < 30.0), curAnglePercent=100 and lightMode=true; loop writes servo 100 and LED HIGH. But io_1 is raw ADC (0-1023) compared to 30.0, so io_1>=30.0 is almost always true, making the light-weak branch unreachable; the LED never turns on and curtain never opens in auto mode.

The temperature check io_1>=30.0 is first in auto mode and sets curtain closed (0) and light off, taking priority over the light branch. The priority structure is implemented; the threshold unit is questionable but the priority ordering itself is present.
Button D2 edge detection toggles autoMode: on rising edge of io_2, autoMode is set to !autoMode. This switches between auto and manual.
In manual mode, button D3 rising edge increments manualAnglePercent by 10, wrapping from 100 to 0; curAnglePercent follows manualAnglePercent and drives the servo. Angle adjustment is implemented.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init, Serial.begin(9600), pinMode(13,OUTPUT) with digitalWrite LOW, pinMode(6,OUTPUT) with noTone(6) (tone command 0), pinMode(8,OUTPUT) LOW, pinMode(9,INPUT). All required pins initialized and approachActive=false gives standby.

When approachActive and flashPhaseMs<100, io_2=true -> digitalWrite(13,HIGH). flashPhaseMs accumulates elapsed and wraps at 200, so LED toggles every 100ms = fast blink. Reachable after trigger sets approachActive=true.
beepSequenceMs accumulates; tone active (2000Hz) when in [0,100),[200,300),[400,500) -> three short beeps within 500ms window, then noTone. Reachable when approachActive.
welcomePulse set true on transition into approachActive, and io_4=welcomePulse; loop prints "welcome" when io_4 true. Pulse is one iteration.
When not detecting (io_1 false or out of range) and approachActive, inactivityMs accumulates; when >=5000, approachActive=false, phases reset -> standby (LED off, no tone).

Serial input is parsed only as tokens T1..T32 mapping to integers 1..32; there is no path to enter arbitrary start and end times. The parsed value io_8 selects fixed presets (1→10/20, 2→30/60), so the system cannot receive and save user-specified start/end times.

Green LED D12 is driven by hw_value_io_6, which equals !occupied && !overtimeActive. There is no comparison of current time to startMin-1 and no blinking logic; D12 is simply steady on when idle. No 1-minute-before reminder exists.

When PIR (io_4) is HIGH, occupied becomes true; then io_7=occupied drives D13 HIGH, and io_3=1 is shown on TM1637 as the number 1, not the text "occupied". The display shows a digit rather than the required word.

overtimeActive is set only when occupied && startMin>0 && endMin>startMin && startMin>=endMin, which is contradictory (endMin>startMin and startMin>=endMin cannot both hold), so overtimeActive is always false. No buzzer tone and no "overtime use" serial output can occur.
Button D7 is read into io_0; on a rising edge (pressed && !prevPressed) occupied and overtimeActive are cleared, releasing the room. This implements manual release.
setup() configures A0, A1, A2 as INPUT, attaches servo to D9, constructs TM1637Display with CLK=4/DIO=5, sets D6 OUTPUT, and sets D2 INPUT_PULLUP. All required devices are initialized.

In auto mode (autoManual false), balance=io_1-io_0; if balance<-35 angle=45, if balance>35 angle=135, else 90. io_0=A0, io_1=A1. When A1>A0 (right brighter) balance>35 gives 135; when A0>A1 gives 45. Servo written to angle. This drives toward stronger side.
lowNow=io_2<614 where io_2 is A2 voltage reading; this determines low charge state. Display alternates between !low and scaled voltage. Charging state is judged from voltage threshold.
Button io_6 (D2, active low debounced) toggles sysml_state_autoManual on rising edge via prevButton. Auto mode when false, manual when true.

alarm=low && (now-lowSince)>=10000, i.e., voltage below threshold for 10s. io_5=alarm?1000:0 drives tone on D6 (1000Hz within 31-65535). serial trigger fires once per low episode, printing "low charge". Both buzzer and serial output occur.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init, configures sensor inputs A1/A0/A2 and button D2, sets outputs D10/D9/D5/D6, initializes TM1637 (clk 4, dio 3) with brightness and a number, and loop() runs the control update each cycle. Initialization and control loop are present.

Heater output io_4 is computed as (water io_2 >= 512) && (io_0 <= 600), where io_0 is A1 (LM35) and io_2 is A2 (water level). The heater is gated by water level, not purely by temperature, and the temperature threshold is applied to the LM35 reading. The requirement is temperature-based heater control; the level gating is an extra condition but the temperature path exists. However the heater is driven by io_0 (A1) which is the LM35, so temperature control is implemented.

Lighting io_5 is set to 1023 when water level io_2 >= 512 and light sensor io_1 <= 512, else 0. io_1 is A0 (photoresistor). analogWrite(9, constrain(io_5,0,255)) drives D9. So lighting responds to ambient light.
Aeration pump io_6 is true when water level io_2 >= 512, else false; digitalWrite(5,...) drives D5. So pump is controlled by water level.

When water level io_2 < 512, io_7 = 2000 (tone on D6) and io_6 = false (pump off). Heater io_4 also requires io_2>=512 so it is off. Lighting io_5 requires io_2>=512 so it is off. So low water turns off devices and sounds buzzer.

Button io_3 edge detection cycles displayModeTemp/Light/Level. However io_8 (display value) is always 0 in all branches (conditional_8/9 all 0), so the TM1637 always shows 0 regardless of mode. The display content does not switch between temperature, light, and water level values.

setup() initializes Serial, A0, A1, D2 (INPUT_PULLUP), D5, D6, D13, and constructs TM1637Display with CLK=4, DIO=3; loop() samples all three inputs and drives outputs each iteration, so real-time monitoring is entered.

With io_2 false, temp<=60 and current<=7, sysml_value_6=0 (normal). But the only status output is the TM1637 number, which shows current/temp for the first 4000ms of each 6000ms cycle; status 0 is only displayed during the last 2000ms window. The normal state is not output as a distinct status during most of the cycle, and no other output encodes 'normal'.

When current>7 and temp<=60 and no vibration, sysml_value_6=1 (overload). This value is only routed to the display during the 4000-6000ms window; during 0-4000ms the display shows current/temp instead. No dedicated overload output exists, so the overload state is not reliably output.

When temp>60, sysml_value_7=255.0 is written to io_3 and analogWrite(5,...) drives D5 to 255, so the fan turns on. The overheat status (2) is computed but only shown on the display in the 4000-6000ms window; the fan cooling requirement is satisfied.

Vibration (io_2 true) sets sysml_value_2=1000 written to io_4, which is passed to tone(6,...) since 1000 is in [31,65535], so the buzzer sounds. faultEntry (rising edge) triggers serial output of fault code 3. Both alarm and fault code are produced.

The status priority chain checks io_2 first (vibration -> 3), so mechanical fault overrides overheat/overload. The buzzer (1000Hz) and fault code 3 are emitted regardless of temp/current, satisfying priority.

displayCycleMs accumulates elapsed ms and wraps at 6000; 0-2000ms shows current (value_0), 2000-4000ms shows temperature (value_1), 4000-6000ms shows status code (value_6). All three are shown in rotation via showNumberDec.

ProgramPage1 computes distancePage=now/2000%2 and writes io_5 as distance when the bit is 1, temperature when 0, so the display alternates every 2 s between temperature and distance (invalid sensor shows -1/clear). The loop calls ProgramPage1 each iteration and updates the TM1637 when io_5 changes, satisfying the alternating display obligation.

hot=io_2 && io_0>32 (strictly above 32). io_6 is set to 1000 only when (hot||near) && now%1000<400, giving a 400 ms on / 600 ms off intermittent tone on D6 via tone(6,1000). serial_0_value_0 is true on the rising edge of hot and every 1000 ms thereafter, and loop prints "ALARM_TEMP". Both intermittent buzzer and serial reason are implemented for temperature >32.

near=io_4 && io_3<15 (strictly below 15 cm, distance computed as pulse/58). The same intermittent tone condition includes near, and serial_0_value_1 triggers on rising edge and every 1000 ms, with loop printing "ALARM_DISTANCE". Both required behaviors are present for distance <15 cm.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init, Serial.begin(9600), pinMode for A0/A1, D2/D3 (INPUT_PULLUP), D12/D13 outputs, TM1637 constructor on D4/D5 with setBrightness, and hw_dht_0.begin()/hw_dht_1.begin() on D7/D8. All required peripherals are initialized and loop() begins polling.

In auto mode (manual false), page=now/2000%6 gives room=page/3 (0 or 1) and metric=page%3 (0,1,2), cycling through both rooms' temperature, humidity, and light every 2s. io_12 is set to data[room][metric] when metric==2 or the room's DHT is valid, and the display shows it via showNumberDec.
D2 (io_8) toggles room and D3 (io_9) advances metric on rising edge, setting manual=true and changed=now; manual auto-clears after 8000ms. Debounced inputs feed these edges.

serial_0_trigger fires when now-lastReport>=5000, and lastReport is updated on trigger. The six report fields (living temp/hum/light, bedroom temp/hum/light) are printed with labels each trigger, giving a full environment report every 5s.

living=io_2 && io_0>32 && io_6>700 and bedroom=io_5 && io_3>32 && io_7>700 drive io_10/io_11, which are written to D12/D13 each loop. On a rising alarm edge serial_1_trigger fires and prints the room-level alarm message. Both LED and message paths are implemented.

Button D2 is read as active-low (digitalRead(2)==LOW) into io_3; ProgramPage1 toggles sysml_state_modeAuto when io_3 is true and previousPressed was false, then stores previousPressed=io_3. So a press toggles the mode with edge detection.

In auto mode, temperatureC = A1*500/1023 (LM35 10mV/°C), autoSpeed maps 20–50°C to 0–255 with clamping, and modeAuto selects autoSpeed into io_2 which drives analogWrite(5). So fan PWM follows temperature in auto mode.
In manual mode, manualLevel = A0*255/1023 and modeAuto false selects manualLevel into io_2, which is written to PWM pin 5. Potentiometer thus controls fan speed in manual mode.
In auto mode io_4 is the truncated integer temperatureC, and loop writes it to the TM1637 via showNumberDec when changed. Display shows current temperature in auto mode.
In manual mode io_4 = floor(manualLevel/10), i.e. a 0–25 level derived from the potentiometer, and loop displays it on the TM1637. This is the manual level shown on the display.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which sets setpointMode_value=false (current-value mode default), and loop() runs ProgramPage1 each iteration with ventilation_enabled set true, so temperature control and periodic ventilation run and display defaults to current value.
When a valid reading io_0 < 37.0, heaterCommand is set true; loop writes D10 HIGH from hw_value_io_2, so heater relay turns on below the lower bound.

When io_0 > 38.0 heaterCommand is set false; between 37.0 and 38.0 inclusive the heater retains its previous state (hysteresis), so at exactly 37.0 or 38.0 the heater is not turned off. The requirement says off at or above the target range, so reaching 37.0 does not turn it off.

ventilation_value is true when ventilation_started and phase<10000; loop writes D5 from hw_value_io_3, so fan runs during the ventilation window. However D5 is also the TM1637 DIO pin per resolved wiring, conflicting with fan output; the fan output path itself is implemented.
On button press (io_7 true and previous false), setpointMode_value toggles; previous is updated each cycle, giving edge-triggered mode switching.
In current-value mode (setpointMode false) with a reading, display value is rounded cachedTemperature; loop shows it on TM1637. Default mode is current value.
In setpoint mode display value is 38, shown on TM1637.
When io_0>38.0 continuously, outsideDuration accumulates to 60000, then alarmActive=true and reportRaised=true; loop drives D13 HIGH, tone on D6 (1000Hz), and prints incubation abnormal once.
The outside condition includes io_0<37.0, so below-lower-bound also accumulates outsideDuration and triggers alarmActive/reportRaised, driving buzzer, LED, and serial message.

After ProgramPage1_Init sets peopleCount=0 and showTempMode=false, loop calls ProgramPage1 which sets io_8=peopleCount=0 (line 128), and the display update writes showNumberDec(0) since previous is INT32_MIN. So the default display shows the count (0).

When entrance (io_1) becomes valid first, lastEntranceValid=true and lastExitValid=false. When exit (io_3) then becomes valid, the branch at line 91 sees lastEntranceValid true and increments peopleCount. So entrance-before-exit increases the count.

When exit (io_3) becomes valid first, lastExitValid=true and lastEntranceValid=false. When entrance (io_1) then becomes valid, the branch at line 91 sees lastEntranceValid false and decrements peopleCount. So exit-before-entrance decreases the count.

Button D2 is read into io_9; on a rising edge (pressed and not previously pressed) showTempMode toggles. When showTempMode is true, io_8 is set to the truncated temperature instead of peopleCount, and the display update writes that value. So pressing D2 switches the display to temperature.

The fan PWM value io_7 is computed solely from peopleCount: 0.0 when count==0, else 100.0. Temperature (tempHold) is never used in the fan computation, so fan speed does not depend on temperature. This contradicts the requirement that fan speed be determined jointly by count and temperature.
When peopleCount==0, sysml_conditional_3 is set to 0.0, io_7 becomes 0.0, and analogWrite(5,0) turns the fan off. So count 0 yields fan off (energy-saving).

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init, Serial.begin(9600), pinMode for A0/A1/2/5/10/6, initializes TM1637Display(4,3) and writes initial outputs; loop() runs the model each cycle. Note D5 is used for both fan PWM and TM1637 DIO per the resolved wiring, but all listed devices are initialized and normal operation begins.

Fan output io_3 is 255 when door closed, not in defrost, and io_0>2500; 128 when door closed, not defrost, io_0<=2500; 0 when door open or in defrost. analogWrite(5,...) applies it. Ambient temperature drives fan on/off (and speed).
inDefrost is set true when io_1>=1000 and otherwise retains previous state (latch), so evaporator temperature triggers defrost entry; io_4 outputs inDefrost to relay D10.

When io_2 (door) is true, doorOpenElapsedMs accumulates io_7 each cycle; when false it resets to 0. Fan is forced to 0 while door open (io_2 true makes lazy_4 false), pausing fan control. Timer accumulates correctly.

alarmLevel set to 1 when io_0>=3000 (ambient over limit) or io_1>=2000; buzzer frequency 1000Hz for level 1, 2000Hz for level>=2; serial prints alarm_level, ambient_temp_c, evap_temp_c, door_open each cycle. Ambient over limit produces level 1 alarm with detailed serial output.
io_1>=2000 sets alarmLevel=1 (severe frost), buzzer 1000Hz, serial detailed output. Note inDefrost also latches at io_1>=1000, but the alarm path for severe frost is present.
When doorOpenElapsedMs>=600000, alarmLevel set to 2, buzzer 2000Hz, serial detailed output. Door timer accumulates while door open. Long door open produces level 2 alarm with detailed status.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init (manualFrozen=false) then writes analogWrite(9, hw_value_io_1) and display with hw_value_io_4, but both are still 0 at setup since ProgramPage1 has not run yet; the first loop iteration then samples A0 and calls ProgramPage1, which in auto mode sets frozenDisplayValue/frozenPwmValue and outputs io_1/io_4 from io_0, then analogWrite(9) and showNumberDec display the mapped value. So after startup the system enters auto mode and drives LED and display from light level.

In auto mode (manualFrozen false), ProgramPage1 computes io_1 and io_4 as floor(io_0) from analogRead(A0) each loop, and loop writes analogWrite(9,...) and showNumberDec(hw_value_io_4). A0 range 0-1023 is passed through constrain to 0-255 for PWM, so light changes alter D9 PWM and the TM1637 number.

On a rising edge of D2 (io_2 true and previousPressed false), manualFrozen toggles to true. Then the auto-update block is skipped, and io_1/io_4 take frozenPwmValue/frozenDisplayValue, so PWM and display freeze at the last auto values.

While manualFrozen is true, another rising edge of D2 toggles manualFrozen back to false; the auto block then recomputes frozenDisplayValue/frozenPwmValue from current io_0 and outputs follow io_0 again, restoring auto mode.

setup() initializes button D3 (INPUT_PULLUP), LED D13 (OUTPUT), buzzer D6 (OUTPUT), vibration D2 (INPUT), water A0 (INPUT), and TM1637 constructed with CLK=4, DIO=5; loop() runs the monitor. All required pins are configured at startup.
phase starts at 1 (fill). io_3=phase is written each loop and displayed via showNumberDec when changed, so the fill stage number 1 is shown on the TM1637.
When phase==1 with water and vibration, phase becomes 2; io_3=phase drives the display to show 2 for the wash stage.
When phase==2 with no water and vibration, phase becomes 3; io_3=phase drives the display to show 3 for the spin stage.
When phase==3 with no vibration for >=2000ms, phase becomes 4; io_3=phase drives the display to show 4 for the end stage.
In phase 4 with !acknowledged, alarm is true; io_1 toggles LED D13 with now%1000<500 and io_2 sets tone 1000Hz on D6 during the same window, so buzzer sounds and LED blinks until acknowledged.
In phase 4, a rising edge on button (io_0 && !previous) sets acknowledged=true; then alarm becomes false, io_1=0 and io_2=0, stopping LED and buzzer.
fault is true when phase!=4, water, no vibration, and idle>=8000ms; serial_0_trigger fires once and loop prints "wash fault" followed by the phase number.

DHT11 on pin 7 is constructed and begun; loop reads it every 2000ms via hw_dht_0.read() and readTemperature(), storing the value in hw_value_io_3 which is passed to ProgramPage1 as io_3. Current temperature is read from D7.

A0 is configured as INPUT and analogRead(A0) is sampled every 10ms into hw_value_io_0, which is passed as io_0 to ProgramPage1 where threshold=(int)(io_0*50.0/1023.0) is computed. Potentiometer determines the threshold.

TM1637Display constructed with CLK=4, DIO=5. io_5 alternates between threshold and current temperature (or -1000 when invalid) based on now/2000%2, and is written via showNumberDec. Both current temperature and threshold are displayed.

io_1 = io_4 && io_3>threshold drives D13 HIGH (steady on) when temp exceeds threshold. io_2 = io_1 && now%1000<400 ? 1000 : 0, so buzzer tone(6,1000) for 400ms each 1000ms cycle while alarm active, and noTone otherwise — periodic alarm. Both conditions satisfied.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init, Serial.begin(9600), pinMode for D2 (2), D3 (3, INPUT_PULLUP), D7 (7, INPUT_PULLUP), D13 (13, OUTPUT), D6 (6, OUTPUT), and constructs TM1637Display with CLK=4, DIO=5. All required devices are initialized.
On D2 rising edge (io_0 true and prevD2 false), totalCount increments by 1 and noProductAccumMs resets. hw_value_io_0 is digitalRead(2)==HIGH, so a product pass increments the count.

Display mode 0 shows totalCount; mode 1 computes achievement rate as totalCount/600*100 (target 600/min) with floor; mode 2 shows stopCount. The TM1637 shows the selected value each loop. However the 'per-minute target' rate is computed as totalCount/600*100, which is a fixed target of 600 per minute, and the display shows cumulative count and rate. This satisfies real-time display of cumulative count and achievement rate.

noProductAccumMs accumulates elapsed ms when no D2 rising edge; when >=30000 and not stopActive, alarmActive=true. On alarm transition, serialGate=true and serialTotalCountI/serialStopCountI are latched, and serial prints total_count, achievement_rate, stop_count — recording the stop event. Alarm also drives D6 tone (2000Hz) and D13 HIGH.

D3 is active-low (digitalRead(3)==LOW). On D3 press edge, stopActive=true and stopCount increments; stopActive forces alarmActive=true, which triggers tone on D6, LED D13 HIGH, and serial event record via serialGate.
When alarmActive, io_4=2000 (tone freq) and io_3=true. Loop writes digitalWrite(13, HIGH) and tone(6, 2000). Both buzzer D6 and LED D13 activate on alarm.
D7 active-low; on press edge displayMode cycles 0→1→2→0. Mode 0 shows totalCount, mode 1 shows achievement rate, mode 2 shows stopCount, and TM1637 displays the selected value.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init, Serial.begin(9600), pinMode for D2/D3 inputs, TM1637 brightness, D6 output, D13 output, D7 INPUT_PULLUP, D8 output, D9 input; loop then runs ProgramPage1 each cycle, entering normal counting state with counters zeroed.

When io_0 (D2 HIGH) is true, alarm not latched, and lastValidDistance < 20 (or no valid distance), countReusable increments. Note the guard uses lastValidDistance>=20 rather than the full-state, but the increment path exists for D2.
When io_1 (D3 HIGH) is true, alarm not latched, and lastValidDistance < 20, countOther increments.
io_4 is set to countReusable+countOther and written to TM1637 via showNumberDec whenever it changes, displaying the total.

When lastValidDistance >= 20, alarmLatched is set true; subsequent increments are gated by !alarmLatched, so counting stops. Alarm outputs: tone 2000 Hz on D6 and LED D13 HIGH. However the full-state comparison uses lastValidDistance>=20 (distance in cm) as 'full', which is a distance threshold, and the counting guard also uses lastValidDistance>=20 rather than alarmLatched alone; still alarm latches and counting stops. The alarm is active.
serial_0_trigger is set to alarmLatched, and loop prints "empty bin needed" followed by the boolean value when triggered.

D7 is read as LOW (pressed). On a rising press edge (prevIo7Pressed false, io_7 true), counters reset to 0, alarmLatched cleared, prevFullState cleared, restoring counting. No explicit 'bin emptied' check, but requirement says reset after clearing; the button resets and counting resumes.

ProgramPage1_Init sets sysml_state_counter=0; setup calls Init then the display block runs with hw_value_io_3=0 (initial static value) and hw_display_previous_io_3=INT32_MIN, so showNumberDec(0,...) executes, displaying 0 at startup.

On a new D2 press (io_0 true, prevIncPressed false) with counter<20, counter increments; io_3 output equals counter (0..20 in range) and loop's display block writes the new value since it differs from previous.
On a new D3 press with counter>0, counter decrements; io_3 reflects the new counter and the display block updates because the value changed.
At counter==20, io_2 becomes 1000 (in 31..65535), so tone(6,1000) sounds the buzzer; the increment branch clamps to 20 so further D2 presses cannot exceed 20.
At counter==0, io_2 becomes 1000, so tone(6,1000) sounds; the decrement branch clamps to 0 so further D3 presses cannot go below 0.

loop() samples A1 every 10ms into hw_value_io_0 (analogRead(A1)*500/1023), passes it to ProgramPage1, which updates sysml_state_maxAdc whenever io_0 exceeds it; maxAdc persists as a global across calls, so the running maximum is retained.

When not showing max, io_2 is set to io_0 (current temperature), and loop writes it to the TM1637 via showNumberDec whenever it differs from the previous value; default state has showMax=false so current temperature is displayed.

On a rising edge of the button (io_1 true, previous false), deadline=millis()+3000 and showMax=true, so io_2 becomes maxAdc and is displayed. After 3000ms, (int32_t)(millis()-deadline)>=0 turns showMax false, restoring io_0 display.
serial_0_trigger is always set true each ProgramPage1 call, and loop prints both current (value_0=io_0) and historical max (value_1=maxAdc) every iteration, so both are continuously output.

setup() calls Serial.begin(9600) and pinMode for D2 (INPUT), D10 (OUTPUT), D6 (OUTPUT), D13 (OUTPUT), D8 (OUTPUT), D9 (INPUT); TM1637 constructed with CLK=4,DIO=5 and setBrightness called. All required pins initialized and serial started.

On rising edge of proximity (io_0 && !previous) with valid level and not low, open=true, opened=now, uses incremented; loop writes D10 HIGH. After 3000ms (now-opened>=3000) open=false and D10 goes LOW. Fixed duration valve activation implemented.

low = !io_3 || percent<20. When low, open is forced false (valve stays off) and io_6=low drives D13 HIGH (LED alarm), and io_5 pulses 1000Hz tone on D6 for 400ms each second. Valve prohibited and alarm triggered.
io_4 alternates every 2s between uses count and percent (now/2000%2 ? uses : percent), and loop writes it to TM1637 via showNumberDec. Both remaining percent and today's use count are displayed.

Serial input is parsed into command buffer; on newline, if command equals "STATUS" the trigger is set, and loop prints today_uses and remaining_percent values. Statistics query over serial returns stats.

D2 is read as active-low (digitalRead(2)==LOW) and debounced; on a rising edge of the debounced value with remainingSeconds<=9989, ProgramPage1 adds 10 to remainingSeconds. The add path is reachable and increments by exactly 10 seconds per press.

D3 is read active-low and debounced; on a rising edge with !running and remainingSeconds>0, running is set true and tick=now, starting the countdown. Reachable via loop calling ProgramPage1 with hw_value_io_1.
remainingSeconds is output via io_3 and written to the TM1637 (CLK=4,DIO=5) with showNumberDec whenever it changes, including each decrement while running. Display shows remaining seconds.
On countdown end, beeping=true and beepStart=now; io_2=1000 while beeping, driving tone(6,1000). After 2000ms beeping=false and io_2=0 -> noTone(6). Buzzer sounds continuously for 2 seconds.

setup() initializes display brightness, pins 13/10/6/2/8/9/11/12, and loop() calls ProgramPage1 then writes display, LEDs, and tone. However the initial display write in setup uses hw_value_io_4=0 and previous=INT32_MIN, so it shows 0; loop then computes displayMode 0 which shows entry distance only when io_1 valid, else 0. Occupancy status is not shown on the display at startup (mode 0 shows entry distance, not parking distance/occupancy). The requirement says display parking distance and occupancy status at startup; the default mode 0 shows entry distance. This contradicts the startup display obligation.

Green LED is pin 10 driven by hw_value_io_6 = sysml_value_2. That is true only when entry valid and entryDistanceCm<30 and NOT (parking valid and parkingDistance<=20). So when a car approaches the entrance (entry<30) and parking is free, green LED turns on. This matches guiding green light on approach.

When parking valid and distance<=20, tone frequency is graded: <10 ->1800, <15 ->1200, else 700; <5 ->2000. Red LED (io_5) is true when parking valid and distance<5, or parking valid and <=20 (with >=5 or not). So red LED on for all parking<=20, and buzzer frequency graded by distance. This satisfies graded buzzer and LED indication.

For parking distance <5 with valid reading, sysml_value_1 (red LED) is true and tone is 2000 Hz continuously (tone() called once, persists). The requirement is continuous alarm under 5cm; tone at 2000 Hz is continuous while condition holds. Satisfied.

Button on D2 read into io_8; on rising edge displayMode increments and wraps at >=3 to 0. Mode 0 shows entry distance (if valid), mode 1 shows parking distance (if valid), mode 2 shows occupiedCount. This cycles entry distance, parking distance, occupancy count. Satisfied.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init, Serial.begin(9600), pinMode(13,OUTPUT), TM1637Display constructed with CLK=4/DIO=5 and setBrightness, DHT constructed with pin 7 DHT11 and begin(). All required initializations present; loop then runs the display cycle.
When valid, value alternates between hw_value_io_1 (temp) and hw_value_io_2 (humidity) based on phase/2000%2, and showNumberDec writes it. Alternation occurs every 2000ms.
When !valid, value=0 and showNumberDec(0,...,4,0) displays 0000. The condition value!=previous or phase<20&&now==phaseStart ensures it is written on failure transition.
digitalWrite(13, !valid && phase%1000<500 ? HIGH : LOW) toggles D13 every 500ms while invalid, producing a blink.
On first read or validity change to invalid, Serial.println("sensor error") is emitted. This covers the failure case.
setup() configures A0 as INPUT, D13 as OUTPUT, D6 as OUTPUT, D8 (Trig) as OUTPUT, D9 (Echo) as INPUT, matching the required wiring and entering a detectable state.

Alarm condition is io_0<500 (dark) AND io_4 (object within 20cm, pulse 116-23200us) AND io_3<=20.0. When all hold, io_1 becomes true (LED on during phase), io_2=2000 (tone), serial trigger true. This triggers the alarm as required.
If io_0>=500 (not dark) or io_4 false (no object) or io_3>20, the lazy chain yields false, so io_1=false, io_2=0, serial trigger false — no alarm.
When alarm active, io_1 is ANDed with phase (millis()%1000<500), so D13 toggles HIGH/LOW every 500ms — blinking.
When alarm active, io_2=2000 gated by phase, so tone(6,2000) is started during phase and noTone(6) when phase ends — intermittent beeping.

When alarm active, serial_0_trigger is true and loop prints 'alarm_distance_cm' plus the distance value. The requirement says output 'alarm'; the printed string is 'alarm_distance_cm', which contains 'alarm' as a prefix but is not exactly 'alarm'. This is a concrete deviation from the required serial output.

modeIsTemp initializes to true in Init and the display value is derived from lastTempC when modeIsTemp is true; with no button press the display shows temperature. However, lastTempC starts at 0.0 and only updates when a valid DHT read occurs (io_2 true), so before first valid read it shows 0, but the default mode is temperature as required.
Button edge detection: on press (io_3 true and previousPressed false) modeIsTemp toggles, and display value switches between temperature and humidity branches. Each press toggles once.
When lastTempC > 30.0, conditional_1 = (temp-30)*20+102, which is >0, so analogWrite(5,...) drives the fan. At exactly 30.0 the else branch gives 0, matching 'higher than 30'.
PWM value increases linearly with temperature above 30 ((temp-30)*20+102), so higher temperature yields higher fan speed, satisfying the requirement.

loop() calls ProgramPage1 each iteration; reportDue is computed from accumulated elapsed ms and serial_0_trigger is overwritten with reportDue, so every ~1000ms the two Serial.print/println pairs emit the A0 light value and A1 temperature value. The 10ms gate and accumulator make the period approximately 1s. Both values are printed on the same trigger.

sysml_value_0 (io_2) is set to (io_0 > lightThreshold) || (io_1 > tempThreshold), and loop writes D13 from hw_value_io_2 every iteration, so the LED lights when either exceeds threshold. However serial_1_trigger is gated by reportDue (line 95), so WARNING is only printed once per second, not immediately on exceedance; the requirement says 'extra output WARNING' when exceeded, and the gating means WARNING is not emitted at the moment of exceedance between report cycles. Also thresholds default to 0.0, so any positive reading triggers. The LED path is correct but the WARNING output is delayed/gated, contradicting the immediate-warning obligation.
setup() calls Serial.begin(9600), pinMode(A1,INPUT), pinMode(5,OUTPUT), pinMode(13,OUTPUT); loop() reads analogRead(A1) into hw_value_io_0 which feeds ProgramPage1. All required init actions present.
SET_THRESHOLD:N parses N (0..100) and encodes 1000+N; ProgramPage1 with io_3_valid and io_3>=1000 sets sysml_state_thresholdC=io_3-1000. Threshold update path is reachable and persists.
SET_FAN_MIN:N parses N (0..255) and encodes 2000+N; ProgramPage1 with io_3_valid and io_3>=2000 sets sysml_state_fanMinPwm=io_3-2000. Fan min update path reachable and persists.
loop reads A1 every 40ms, ProgramPage1 computes temperature=io_0*500/1023, speed=fanMin+max(0,diff)*25, clamps to 255, and analogWrite(5,...) applies it each iteration. PWM tracks temperature.

io_2=difference>=5.0 drives digitalWrite(13,HIGH) each loop; serial_0_trigger fires on rising edge and prints "overheat_temperature" plus value. LED and overheat warning both produced when temp exceeds threshold by >=5.

setup() configures D13 output, D9 output with analogWrite, D8 output LOW, D2 input, and constructs TM1637Display(4,5) with setBrightness. However the ultrasonic Echo is wired to D2 per resolved_devices, not D9 as the checklist states; the checklist's Echo=D9 conflicts with the authoritative wiring. The code uses pulseIn(2,...) matching D2. The required devices are initialized for operation (Trig D8, Echo D2, TM1637 D4/D5, D13, D9 PWM).
After ProgramPage1 computes hw_value_io_2 (truncated distance), loop compares to previous and calls showNumberDec when changed, so measured distance is displayed on TM1637.
ProgramPage1 sets io_3 true when io_1 (valid measurement) and io_0 <= 30.0; loop writes D13 HIGH/LOW from hw_value_io_3, so D13 lights at close range.

For valid measurement with distance <=30, io_4 = (30-distance)/30*255, giving higher PWM for closer distance; beyond 30 it is 0. analogWrite(9,...) applies it. Monotonic decreasing brightness with increasing distance.

setup() configures A0 as INPUT, D2 as INPUT_PULLUP, D9 as OUTPUT with analogWrite, and D8 as OUTPUT (Trig) with D3 as INPUT (Echo). However the requirement specifies Echo=D9, but the code uses D3 for pulseIn and D9 for the PWM LED, so the HC-SR04 Echo pin is not on D9 as required.

In auto mode (modeForced false), io_3 becomes 255 only when io_0>=0.0 (always true for analogRead) AND io_5 (person detected) AND io_4>0.0. io_5 is set true only when pulse in [116,23200], and io_4 is set to pulse/58 only when io_5 true, so io_4>0.0 holds. Thus dark+person yields analogWrite(9,255). But the darkness condition io_0>=0.0 is always true regardless of light level, so the 'environment dark' requirement is not actually enforced; LED lights whenever a person is detected. This contradicts the required dark AND person condition.

When no person is detected (io_5 false), io_3=0 and analogWrite(9,0), so LED off — that part is correct. But when environment is not dark, io_0>=0.0 is still true (analogRead always >=0), so with a person present the LED still lights at 255. The 'not dark' branch does not turn the LED off, violating the requirement.
Button on D2 read as active-low (digitalRead==LOW). Edge detection via previousPressed toggles modeForced on each new press. This implements toggling between forced and auto modes.
When modeForced is true, io_3 is set to 255.0 unconditionally, ignoring light and proximity, so LED stays at full brightness.
D2 press with running=false: io_0 rising edge triggers running=!running, so running becomes true; elapsed then accumulates dt each call, so seconds start counting.
D2 press while running=true: same edge toggles running to false, so elapsed stops accumulating; timer pauses.
D3 press edge sets elapsed=0, running=false, beeping=false; io_3=elapsed/1000 becomes 0 and display updates.
io_3=elapsed/1000 is written to TM1637 via showNumberDec when changed; while running elapsed grows so displayed seconds update.
At 60s crossing beeping=true and beepStart=now; io_2=1000 maps to tone(6,1000) for 1s, then beeping=false and noTone; elapsed keeps accumulating so timing continues.

ProgramPage1_Init sets sysml_state_modeAuto=true and manualThresholdCm=15.0; in auto mode the alarm comparison uses the literal 15.0 (io_3 < 15.0), so at startup the system is in auto mode with a fixed 15cm alarm distance.

In auto mode the threshold comparison is hardcoded io_3 < 15.0 and the displayed threshold is the literal 15; the potentiometer value io_0 is only used inside the button-press branch to compute manualThresholdCm, so auto mode is unaffected by A0.

On a button press the code computes manualThresholdCm from io_0 (A0 reading) via io_0*400/1023, and in manual mode the alarm comparison uses io_3 < sysml_state_manualThresholdCm, so the threshold is set by the potentiometer.

Button D2 is read as active-low (digitalRead(2)==LOW) into io_1; on a rising edge of pressed (io_1 true and previousPressed false) the code toggles sysml_state_modeAuto, and previousPressed is updated each cycle, giving edge-triggered mode switching.
io_5 is set to 15 in auto mode or the floored manualThresholdCm in manual mode, and loop writes it to the TM1637 via showNumberDec when it changes, so the display shows the current threshold.

ProgramPage1 sets *serial_0_trigger=report where report is true on first call and every >=3000ms via millis() accumulator; loop prints Temperature and Distance when trigger set. Temperature comes from DHT read (io_1/io_3) and distance from ultrasonic (io_4/io_5), both polled in loop. The 3s cadence is implemented via the report accumulator, satisfying the periodic poll and serial output obligation.

On each report, if io_5 valid and io_4<20, closeCount increments up to 3; when it reaches 3, serial_1_trigger is set and *io_0=closeCount>=3 drives D13 HIGH. loop prints "persistent object detected" on serial_1_trigger and writes D13 from hw_value_io_0. Three consecutive sub-20cm readings thus light LED and print the message.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init (lightOn=false, count=0), configures D2/D3 as INPUT_PULLUP, D13 as OUTPUT driven LOW, D6 as OUTPUT with noTone (tone command 0), and initializes TM1637 on pins 4/5 with brightness; the display block runs because hw_value_io_4 (0) != INT32_MIN, showing 0. All devices initialized and display shows count 0.
D2 is read as active-low (digitalRead(2)==LOW) into io_0; on rising edge (io_0 && !previous[0]) lightOn=true and count++. Output io_2 drives digitalWrite(13,HIGH), lighting the LED.
D3 read active-low into io_1; on rising edge lightOn=false and count++, then digitalWrite(13,LOW) turns the LED off.
hw_rx_parse maps "LIGHT_ON" to 6; ProgramPage1 with io_5_valid and io_5==6 sets lightOn=true and increments count; output drives D13 HIGH.
"LIGHT_OFF" maps to 5; io_5==5 sets lightOn=false and increments count; D13 driven LOW.

"BEEP" maps to 1; io_5==1 sets beeping=true and beepStart=millis(), count++. Output io_3=1000 while beeping, and the tone block calls tone(6,1000) since 1000 is in [31,65535] and differs from hw_tone_io_3 (-1). After 200ms beeping clears, io_3=0, noTone(6).
"COUNT_RESET" maps to 3; io_5==3 sets sysml_state_count=0; io_4 output becomes 0, differs from previous, and showNumberDec displays 0.

Each local button edge (lines 52-53) and each LIGHT_ON/LIGHT_OFF/BEEP command (lines 55-57) increments sysml_state_count; COUNT_RESET does not. io_4 carries count to the display block which shows it when changed.

setup() initializes TM1637 (CLK=4,DIO=5 via constructor), LED D13 as OUTPUT, buzzer D6 as OUTPUT, Trig D8 as OUTPUT, Echo D9 as INPUT; loop() performs periodic ultrasonic measurement (60ms) and calls ProgramPage1 to drive display/LED/buzzer. All required pins are configured and the ranging/display loop runs.
ProgramPage1 computes sysml_value_0 as floor of lastValidDistanceCm and writes to *io_2; loop() then calls showNumberDec with hw_value_io_2 when it changes, displaying the distance on TM1637.
sysml_value_1 = (lastValidDistanceCm < 30.0) is written to *io_3, and loop() drives D13 HIGH when hw_value_io_3 is true, so distance <30cm lights the LED.

For 8<=d<15, sysml_value_2=140, then line 70 gates to 1000 only when millis()%1000<100, producing a slow beep (100ms on per 1s). tone(6,1000) is applied. This matches slow beep for <15cm (and also for <8cm the period changes to 250ms, faster).
For d<8, sysml_value_2=220, period=250ms, so beep is 100ms on per 250ms — faster than the 1s period used for 8-15cm. tone(6,1000) applied. This is a rapid beep for <8cm.

Button press (io_1 true, previousPressed false) advances pageIndex 0→1→2→0; display value selects io_0 (light) for page 0, temp for page 1, humidity for page 2, and showNumberDec is called when the value changes. All three pages are reachable and displayed.

reportDue is computed as accum+elapsed>=2000 before adding elapsed, and serial_0_trigger is overwritten with reportDue at line 194. The accumulator is reset by subtracting 2000, so trigger fires when accumulated elapsed reaches 2000ms. All three values (io_0, temp, hum) are printed under the trigger. The 2-second period is implemented via the accumulator.

No code anywhere compares illumination to a low threshold or temperature to a high threshold, and no abnormal-environment message is printed. The serial output only prints the three values; there is no conditional warning branch.

When analogRead(A1) yields a value <=100 (e.g. 0), ProgramPage1 sets fanLevel=0, sysml_value_0=0 (PWM 0 = off), and sysml_value_2=0. loop writes analogWrite(5,0) and showNumberDec(0) since 0 differs from INT32_MIN, so fan off and display shows 0.
For 100<io_0<=200, fanLevel=1, sysml_conditional_1=85.0, sysml_conditional_0=85.0, so analogWrite(5,85) low speed; sysml_value_2=1 displayed via showNumberDec(1).
For 200<io_0<=300, fanLevel=2, sysml_conditional_2=170.0, then sysml_conditional_1=170.0 and sysml_conditional_0=170.0, so analogWrite(5,170) medium; display shows 2.
For io_0>300, fanLevel=3, else branch sets sysml_conditional_2=255.0, sysml_conditional_1=255.0, sysml_conditional_0=255.0, so analogWrite(5,255) high; display shows 3.

On transition into fanLevel 3, high && !wasHigh sets beepStart=millis(); sysml_value_1=2000 (valid tone freq) so tone(6,2000) starts. After 200ms, *io_3=0 but io_2 remains 2000, so tone continues indefinitely rather than a short beep; the beep is not stopped. Also io_3 (display) is overwritten to 0, so display shows 0 instead of 3 during high. The short-beep obligation is not met.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which sets led1/led2 false, and hw_value_io_0/io_1 are static-initialized false; digitalWrite(2,LOW) and digitalWrite(3,LOW) drive both pins low at power-on, so both LEDs are off.
loop computes phase = millis()%20000 and sets io_0 = phase>=5000 && phase<15000, so at 5000ms pin 2 goes HIGH turning LED1 on.
io_1 = phase>=10000 && phase<15000, so at 10000ms pin 3 goes HIGH turning LED2 on while LED1 remains on.
At phase=15000 both conditions become false, so io_0 and io_1 both go LOW in the same loop iteration, driving pins 2 and 3 low simultaneously.
phase wraps modulo 20000, so from 15000 to 20000 both outputs stay LOW (5s off), then at phase 0 the cycle restarts with LED1 off until 5000ms again, repeating the sequence.
setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which resets state, and all hw_value_io_2_segment_* globals are false-initialized; setup writes LOW to pins 2-11, so all bar graph LEDs are off at power-on/reset.

count=(int)(io_0*10/1023). Segment_9 drives pin 11 (A10) with count>0, segment_8 pin 10 with count>1, etc. As pot increases, count rises and LEDs light starting from pin 11 (A10) upward, matching the required first-LED order.
As count decreases, the highest-index segments (pin 11 first) turn off first, leaving fewer LEDs lit starting from the first LED (A10/pin 11).

On button press (io_1 rising edge), reverse toggles true. Then segment_0 (pin 2, A1) lights when count>0, segment_1 when count>1, etc., so lighting starts from A1 (last LED) with count still matching pot value.
Second press toggles reverse back to false, restoring the original order where segment_9 (A10) lights first.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which sets digit=9, and hw_value_io_2 is statically initialized to 9, so the shift register is written with digit 9 in setup. hw_value_io_0 and hw_value_io_1 are false, so pins 2 and 3 are driven LOW, turning both LEDs off. Display shows 9 and both LEDs off at power-on.

io_0 = millis()/2000%2==0 and io_1 = !io_0, so at t=0 io_0=true (led1 on), io_1=false. At t=2000 io_0=false, io_1=true (led2 on). At t=4000 io_0=true again. Alternating 2-second interval with led1->led2->led1 sequence, one on while other off.
io_2 = 9-(millis()/4000%10). At t=0 digit=9, t=4000 digit=8, ... t=36000 digit=0, t=40000 digit=9. Decrements every 4 seconds from 9 to 0.
At millis()=40000, millis()/4000%10 = 0, so io_2 = 9-0 = 9, resetting to 9 and restarting the countdown.
When io_2 changes, the loop detects the difference and calls hw_shift595_io_2 immediately in the same iteration, updating the shift register output.

LED outputs are computed from millis() independently of the countdown, and loop() runs continuously updating pins 2 and 3 every iteration regardless of digit changes, so blinking continues throughout the countdown.
setup() calls Serial.begin(9600), pinMode(13,OUTPUT), pinMode(9,OUTPUT), pinMode(6,OUTPUT), pinMode(2,INPUT_PULLUP), initializing all four devices and serial.
Command "ON" sets mode=1; io_0 = (mode==1) is true, and loop writes digitalWrite(13,HIGH), lighting the LED.
Command "OFF" sets mode=0; io_0 evaluates false (mode!=1 and mode!=2), so digitalWrite(13,LOW) turns the LED off.
Command "BLINK" sets mode=2 and blinkStart=now; io_0 toggles based on (now-blinkStart)%1000<500, producing a 500ms on/off blink written to pin 13.
PWM:value parses with strtol, validates 0..255, stores in sysml_state_pwmValue; io_1 outputs it and analogWrite(9,...) applies it.
Command "BUZZ" sets buzzing=true; io_2=1000 while buzzing, and loop calls tone(6,1000) since 1000 is within 31..65535, driving the buzzer.
Command "STATUS" sets report=true; loop prints LED_STATE and PWM_VALUE via Serial when trigger is set.
Button on D2 read as (digitalRead==LOW) with debounce; report=io_3 && !prevPressed triggers on press edge, printing LED_STATE and PWM_VALUE.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which sets muted=false (default non-muted), configures pinMode 2 INPUT, 13 OUTPUT, 6 OUTPUT, 8 OUTPUT, 9 INPUT, matching Trig=D8, Echo=D9, buzzer D6, button D2, LED D13. All required initialization present.
When not muted, io_3 distance selects frequency: <10→2000, <20→1500, <30→1000, else 500. loop writes tone(6, freq) when command changes. Distance-dependent frequency implemented.
Edge detection: on io_0 high with previousPressed false, toggles sysml_state_muted; previousPressed updated each call. Button press toggles mute state.
When muted, sysml_value_0=true → io_1=true → digitalWrite(13,HIGH) each loop, LED stays on.
Serial trigger is io_4 (ultrasonic valid), independent of muted state; when valid, distance printed regardless of mute. Muting only zeroes frequency, not serial trigger.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init, configures A0 as INPUT, D2/D3 as INPUT_PULLUP, constructs TM1637Display(4,5) and DHT(7,DHT11) with begin(), and loop() drives the menu state machine, so all devices are initialized and the menu system runs.
On D2 press (io_1 true and previous false), menuIndex increments with wraparound 2->0, cycling among the three menu items.
On D3 press (io_2 true and previous false), confirmedIndex is set to the current menuIndex, confirming the selected item.
When confirmedIndex==0 and tempValid, the temperature is scaled by 10 and rounded, output to io_6, and displayed; it persists each loop until confirmedIndex changes via D3.
When confirmedIndex==1 and tempValid, humidity is scaled by 10 and rounded, output to io_6 and displayed, persisting until confirmedIndex changes.
When confirmedIndex is neither 0 nor 1 (i.e., 2), the else branch reads io_0 (potentiometer A0) and outputs its integer value to io_6, displayed and persisting until confirmedIndex changes.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init, configures A0 INPUT, D2 INPUT_PULLUP, D13 OUTPUT, and constructs TM1637Display(4,5) with setBrightness; loop() runs the update and drives LED and display, entering the running system.

analogRead(A0) is sampled into hw_value_io_0 and passed to ProgramPage1, where period=100+(int)(io_0*900.0/1023.0) is computed each call and used in the modulo blink expression, so the blink period tracks the pot reading.
ProgramPage1 outputs period via *io_3, and loop() writes it to the TM1637 with showNumberDec when it changes, so the display shows the current period value.

On a rising edge of the debounced button (io_1 && !previousPressed), running is toggled; when stopped (running false) a press sets running true, and io_2 becomes the blink expression, driving D13 to blink.
When running is true, a button press toggles it to false; io_2 then evaluates false (running && ...), so blinking stops.
When stopped, io_2 is false, and loop() writes digitalWrite(13, hw_value_io_2 ? HIGH : LOW), driving D13 LOW (off).
Stopping only toggles running; period is recomputed from the pot each call and not reset, and the display continues to show the current period, so the period setting is retained while stopped.

At setup, hw_value_io_1=0 and hw_shift595_previous_io_1=INT32_MIN, so hw_shift595_io_1(0) runs, shifting digits[0]=0x3f for both units and tens, which is the '0' pattern for both sevseg1 and sevseg2. hw_value_io_2/3/4 are false, so pins 2,3,4 are driven LOW, turning all LEDs off. This satisfies the power-on/reset state.
analogRead(A3) yields 0..1023, and ProgramPage1 computes value=(int)(io_0*99.0/1023.0), mapping 0->0 and 1023->99, giving 0..99. This matches the required mapping.

hw_shift595_io_1 shifts the units digit (value/1%10) first into sr1, then the tens digit (value/10%10) into sr2 via daisy chain, so sevseg1 shows tens and sevseg2 shows units. The bit inversion matches the common-anode wiring where MR is tied to VCC.
io_2 is always set true, so pin 2 (led1) is always HIGH. For value 0..33, io_3=value>=34 is false and io_4=value>=67 is false, so led2 and led3 are off. Only led1 lights, satisfying the requirement.
For value 34..66, io_2=true (led1 on), io_3=value>=34 true (led2 on), io_4=value>=67 false (led3 off). Both led1 and led2 light, matching the requirement.
For value 67..99, io_2=true, io_3=true, io_4=value>=67 true, so pins 2,3,4 all HIGH and all three LEDs light. Satisfies the requirement.
loop samples A3 every 5ms, recomputes value, and updates the shift register (on change) and pins 2/3/4 each iteration, so displays and LEDs track the potentiometer continuously.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init (displayNumber=0) then hw_shift595_io_1(0) since previous is INT32_MIN. For value 0, units digit 0 -> digits[0]=0x3f, tens digit 0 -> 0x3f. Both shiftOut calls write the same inverted pattern; the second overwrites the first, so both sevseg1 and sevseg2 receive the '0' pattern. Displays show "00".
In setup, hw_value_io_5 is false (static init), so digitalWrite(4, LOW). Pin 4 is bargraph1:A1. So A1 is LOW, not lit. The bar graph segment A1 does not light at initialization.
setup writes digitalWrite(2, hw_value_io_3?HIGH:LOW) and digitalWrite(3, hw_value_io_4?HIGH:LOW). Both hw_value_io_3 and hw_value_io_4 are false statics, so both pins LOW. LEDs off.
number = (millis()/2000)%100. At t=0..1999 number=0; at t=2000..3999 number=1; increments by 1 every 2 seconds. The loop's 10ms gate doesn't affect the 2s boundary materially.
tick%100 wraps: at tick=99 number=99, at tick=100 number=0. Resets to 00 after 99.
hw_shift595_io_1 writes units digit first then tens digit; the second shiftOut overwrites the first, so both displays get the tens digit. sevseg2 (units) shows tens digit, not units. Wrong mapping.

count=number/10+1. io_5=count>0 always true (count>=1), io_6=count>1, ... io_14=count>9. For number 0-9 count=1 -> only io_5 (pin4/A1) on. For 25 count=3 -> io_5,io_6,io_7 on (3 segments). For 90 count=10 -> all 10 on. Matches tens+1 segments.

io_3=tick && tick%2, io_4=tick && !(tick%2). At tick=0 both false (both off). At tick=1: io_3=1, io_4=0 (led1 on, led2 off). At tick=2: io_3=0, io_4=1 (led1 off, led2 on). Alternates every 2 seconds. Initial both off is acceptable per example.

In setup, hw_value_io_0 is -1 and hw_shift595_previous_io_0 is INT32_MIN, so the condition is true and hw_shift595_io_0(-1) is called. value=-1 fails valid (value>=0), so segments=0, bits=0, then bits=~0=0xFF, shiftOut sends 0xFF. With common anode (MR tied to VCC via COM), 0xFF means all segments off. Display is off at power-on.

ProgramPage1 computes millis()/2000%3. At t=0..1999ms this is 0, digits[0]=0x3f which is segments A-F (0). The loop calls hw_shift595_io_0(0) on first iteration, outputting ~0x3f=0xC0, lighting segments for '0'.
At t=2000..3999ms, millis()/2000%3 = 1, digits[1]=0x77 which is segments A,B,C,E,F,G = 'A'. Output ~0x77 lights those segments.

At t=4000..5999ms, millis()/2000%3 = 2, digits[2]=0x73 which is segments A,B,C,E,F,G minus D... 0x73 = 0b1110011 = A,B,C,E,F,G? 0x73 bits: 1,2,16,32,64 = A,B,E,F,G plus 0x10=E? Let me check: 0x73=0b1110011: bit0(A)=1,bit1(B)=1,bit4(E)=1,bit5(F)=1,bit6(G)=1, bit2(C)=0,bit3(D)=0. That's A,B,E,F,G = 'P' (no C,D). Correct.
The modulo 3 wraps: at t=6000ms, millis()/2000%3 = 3%3 = 0, returning to '0'. The loop runs continuously and re-evaluates each iteration, so the sequence repeats.
At startup hw_value_io_0=false and hw_value_io_1=true; setup writes pin2 LOW (led1 off) and pin3 HIGH (led2 on) before any loop toggling. Matches required initial state.

io_0=tick%2 and io_1=!io_0 with tick=now/2000, so each LED alternates every 2s and they are always complementary. However the requirement says each LED stays on 2s and off 2s; with tick%2 each LED is on 2s then off 2s, which matches. Alternation and complement hold.
io_2=tick%10 with tick=now/2000 gives 0..9 each for 2s then resets to 0. Matches.

angle uses phase=now%12000: 0-4000ms ramps 0→180 (4s), 4000-6000 holds 180 (2s), 6000-10000 ramps 180→0 (4s), 10000-12000 holds 0 (2s). The sweep 0→180 takes 4s and 180→0 takes 4s, matching 'each sweep taking 4 seconds'.
io_4=180-angle, so servo2 starts at 180, ramps to 0 over 4s, holds 0 for 2s, ramps back to 180 over 4s, holds 180 for 2s. Matches 180→0→180 with 4s sweeps.
io_3=angle and io_4=180-angle are computed from the same phase each loop, so they move in opposite directions simultaneously.
The phase schedule holds 180 for 4000-6000ms and holds 0 for 10000-12000ms, i.e., a 2s pause at each endpoint after a sweep. Matches.

At startup phase=0 gives angle=0 and io_4=180, and the first 0-4000ms segment immediately ramps without any hold at the start. The 2s holds only occur at 4000-6000 and 10000-12000, not before the first sweep. Matches.

All outputs are computed each loop from millis() with no blocking delays; LEDs, shift register display, and both servos are updated in the same loop iteration, so they operate simultaneously and independently.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init setting count=0, alarmLocked=false; hw_value_io_2 defaults false so D13 is written LOW at setup. In loop, ProgramPage1 computes sysml_value_0: for count==0 conditional_4=true, so io_2=true → D13 HIGH. For count=1, the else branch computes conditional_4 = (count == 2 + (floor(count/2)-cond5)*0) = (count==2), false → LED LOW. For count=2, count==2 true → LED HIGH. So even→HIGH, odd→LOW. Display shows count via showNumberDec. Matches requirement.

When not locked and D2 pressed with rising edge (io_0 true, prevUp false), if count==15 sets alarmLocked=true and count=15 (no increment), else count=count+1. For count<15, increments and display updates via showNumberDec since value changes. Requirement says D2 adds one when not locked; at count 15 it locks instead of incrementing, which is the alarm behavior. For normal counts increment works.

When not locked and D3 pressed with rising edge, if count==0 sets count=15 (wrap), else count=count-1. Display updates on change. Decrement works for count>0. At count 0 it wraps to 15 rather than going negative, which is a design choice; requirement just says D3 decrements. The wrap at 0 is arguably a deviation but the decrement path exists. However at count 0 pressing D3 sets count to 15, not -1; requirement doesn't specify wrap behavior. The decrement for count>0 is implemented.

After count changes, loop recomputes io_2 and writes D13. For count=1 (odd) conditional_4 = (1==2) false → LOW. For count=2 (even) true → HIGH. For count=3: floor(3/2)=1, cond5: 1.5<1 false so cond5=0, conditional_4=(3==2+1*0=2) false → LOW. For count=4: floor=2, 2<2 false cond5=0, (4==2) false → LOW! Wait: count=4 even should be HIGH but formula gives (4==2) false. Let me recompute: conditional_4 = count == (2 + (floor(count/2) - cond5)*0). The *0 makes the whole term 0, so it's count==2. So only count==2 gives true (plus count==0). So count=4 → false → LED LOW, but 4 is even and should be HIGH. This is a bug: LED only lights for count 0 and 2, not all even counts.

When count reaches 15 via D2 increment: at count==15 the branch sets alarmLocked=true and count=15. Then io_3 = 1000 (tone freq) since alarmLocked, so tone(6,1000) plays buzzer. While locked, the else branch is skipped so D2/D3 don't change count. Matches requirement.

When alarmLocked and D3 pressed with rising edge (io_1 true, prevDown false), sets alarmLocked=false and count=0. This is a single press, not a long press. Requirement says long press D3 to reset. The code resets on any rising edge of D3, not requiring a long press. This is a deviation: no long-press timing implemented.

setup() initializes all output pins using the zero-initialized static globals: hw_value_io_1..3 are 0 so analogWrite(5/6/7,0) drives RGB channels off, and hw_value_io_4..6 are false so digitalWrite(2/3/4,LOW) keeps led1/led2/led3 off. All LEDs are off at reset before any loop iteration.
For io_0 <= 341, sysml_value_3 (io_4) is true and sysml_value_4/5 are false, so digitalWrite(2,HIGH), digitalWrite(3,LOW), digitalWrite(4,LOW): only led1 on. Boundary 341 included.
For 342 <= io_0 <= 682, sysml_value_4 (io_5) is true and io_4/io_6 false, so digitalWrite(3,HIGH) and pins 2,4 LOW: only led2 on. Both boundaries included.
For io_0 >= 683, sysml_value_5 (io_6) is true and io_4/io_5 false, so digitalWrite(4,HIGH) and pins 2,3 LOW: only led3 on.
For io_0 <= 341, sysml_value_0 = 255.0 written to io_1, and loop writes analogWrite(5,255) — red channel at max. Other channels are 0 in this range.
For 342 <= io_0 <= 682, sysml_value_1 = 255.0 written to io_2, and loop writes analogWrite(6,255) — green channel at max.
For io_0 >= 683, sysml_value_2 = 255.0 written to io_3, and loop writes analogWrite(7,255) — blue channel at max.
loop() re-reads A3 every 5ms into hw_value_io_0, calls ProgramPage1 to recompute outputs, and writes all six pins each pass, so LED states track the current potentiometer value continuously.
setup() initializes all hw_value_* flags to false and writes LOW to every output pin (2-13,44,45) before loop() runs, so all LEDs including bargraph segments start off.
At millis 0-1999 stage=0, mask=1: io_0=0 (led1 off), io_1=1 (rgb1 R on), io_2..io_9=0 (rgb1 G/B, rgb2, rgb3 off), segment_0=1 only (pin12/A1). Matches Stage 1.
Stage=1, mask=34 (0b100010): io_0=1 (led1 on), io_1=0,io_2=1 (rgb1 green), io_3=0; io_4=0,io_5=1 (rgb2 blue), io_6=0; io_7..io_9=0 (rgb3 off); segments 0,1 on (A1-A2). Matches Stage 2.
Stage=2, mask=140 (0b10001100): io_0=0 (led1 off), io_1=0,io_2=0,io_3=1 (rgb1 blue); io_4=1,io_5=0,io_6=0 (rgb2 red); io_7=1,io_8=0,io_9=0 (rgb3 green); segments 0,1,2 on (A1-A3). Matches Stage 3.
Stage=3, mask=511 (all 9 bits set): io_0=1 (led1 on), io_1..io_9 all 1 (all RGB white); segments 0-3 all on (A1-A4). Matches Stage 4.
stage=millis()/2000UL%4 gives each stage exactly 2000ms; loop updates every ~10ms so transitions occur at 2000,4000,6000,8000ms. Each stage lasts 2 seconds.
The %4 in stage computation wraps stage 3 back to 0 at 8000ms, restarting Stage 1 outputs (mask=1, led1 off, rgb1 red, one segment). Sequence repeats.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which sets displayedNumber=0, tensDigit=0, unitsDigit=0. hw_value_io_0/1/2 are static false, so pins 2,3,4 are written LOW (LEDs off). hw_value_io_3 is 0, so hw_shift595_io_3(0) shifts digit 0 for both displays (showing '00'). Servos: hw_value_io_4/5/6 are static 0.0, so attach then write(0) for all three servos. All init conditions satisfied.

loop accumulates hw_elapsed into sysml_state_elapsedAccumMs each iteration (>=10ms gate). When accumulator >=2000, subtract 2000 and increment displayedNumber. First increment occurs at ~2000ms after first loop step; subsequent increments every ~2000ms. Increment by 1 satisfied.
After increment, if displayedNumber > 99 it is set to 0. So 99->100->0. Reset to 0 when exceeding 99 satisfied.
unitsDigit computed as displayedNumber - 10*tensDigit. For units 0-2, sysml_lazy_3 true -> io_0 true, io_1/io_2 false. digitalWrite(2,HIGH), 3/4 LOW. Only led1 on.
For units 3-5, sysml_lazy_5 true -> io_1 true, io_0/io_2 false. Only led2 (pin 3) on.
For units 6-9, sysml_lazy_7 true -> io_2 true, io_0/io_1 false. Only led3 (pin 4) on.
tensDigit 0-2: io_4=30, io_5=60, io_6=90. Servo writes gated by range 0-180 and change detection; values applied.
tensDigit 3-5: lazy_10 true -> io_4=60, io_5=90, io_6=120.
tensDigit 6-9: lazy_10 false -> io_4=90, io_5=120, io_6=150.
After ProgramPage1 updates displayedNumber, io_3=displayedNumber; loop compares to previous and calls hw_shift595_io_3 immediately in same iteration, updating both displays.

On a debounced press (io_0 rising edge), pressed is true; sampleCount increments, serial_0_trigger is set true, and loop prints light (A0 raw), temp (A1 scaled), and count. However the light value printed is the raw A0 reading (io_1) and temp is io_2*500/1023, both sampled in loop before the call; the trigger fires the same iteration so a reading is acquired and output. The count increments by one and is printed. This satisfies the obligation.

When sampleCount%5==0 on a press, beepStart=millis() and beeping=true; io_3=beeping drives D6 HIGH. On subsequent loop iterations, once millis()-beepStart>=200, beeping=false and D6 goes LOW, producing a ~200ms beep every 5th sample. The beep is emitted on the 5th, 10th, etc. sample. This satisfies the short beep requirement.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which sets count=0, then hw_value_io_0 is 0 and differs from INT32_MIN, so hw_shift595_io_0(0) writes digits[0]=0x3f. The bits are inverted (~0x3f=0xC0) and shifted out; with common-anode wiring (MR tied to VCC via COM), inverted bits drive segments A-F on to display 0. Display shows 0 at power-on.
On a debounced press (stable becomes true), count=(count+3)%12. From 0: 3, 6, 9, then 12%12=0. Increment is by 3 each press.

Modulo is %12, not %10. From 9, next press gives (9+3)%12=0, which does wrap to 0. However from 6, next is 9, then 0. The wrap point: after reaching 9, next press yields 0. This matches 'wrap around to 0 after reaching 9'. But note count can only be 0,3,6,9; 9+3=12%12=0. Satisfies.
After ProgramPage1 updates hw_value_io_0, loop compares to previous and calls hw_shift595_io_0 immediately in same iteration, updating display.

ProgramPage1 implements 25ms debounce: raw change resets changed timer, stable only updates after 25ms of consistent reading, and increment only on stable rising edge. Prevents multiple increments per press.
Display is updated whenever hw_value_io_0 changes, using digits table indexed by value%10. Values 0,3,6,9 all map correctly. Display reflects current count after each press.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init, Serial.begin(9600), pinMode(A1,INPUT), pinMode(2,INPUT), pinMode(3,INPUT), constructs TM1637Display(4,5) with brightness, pinMode(6,OUTPUT) for buzzer, pinMode(13,OUTPUT) for LED, and loop() runs the monitoring update. All required devices are initialized and monitoring begins.

Temperature is computed as io_0*500/1023 (LM35 10mV/°C scaled), warm=temperature>8. On rising warm, a log line with label and GPS position is printed. io_4=1000 (tone) and io_5=true (LED HIGH) whenever warm, so buzzer and LED activate. Temperature abnormal is logged via the rising-edge event. This satisfies immediate alarm plus position log plus temperature record.

io_2 is digitalRead(3) (door). On rising door (io_2 && !prevDoor) a 'box opened' log with GPS position is printed. io_4=1000 and io_5=true when io_2 is high, so buzzer and LED activate immediately. Door event is recorded via the rising-edge log.
