io_1 is digitalRead(2) (vibration). On rising shock (io_1 && !prevShock) a 'shock' log is printed and events counter increments. However the requirement is to record the count of severe vibrations; the code increments a generic 'events' counter shared with temperature and door events, not a dedicated vibration count. sysml_state_vibrationCount is declared but never incremented. The vibration count is not separately recorded.

io_3 alternates between events and temperature based on now/2000%2, and the display shows io_3 via showNumberDec. So it alternates between current temperature and the abnormal/event count. This satisfies alternating display of temperature and abnormal count.

Event logs print ' GPS: ' followed by manualLatitude,manualLongitude when manualLocationValid, which is set by parsing 'GPS:lat,lon' serial input. So logs include position from GPS simulated serial data.

setup() writes hw_value_io_0=false to pin 2 (led1 off), and hw_value_io_1/4/7=true, io_2/5/8=false, io_3/6/9=false, so rgb R pins (3,6,9) HIGH, G (4,7,10) and B (5,8,11) LOW = Red on all three. First loop iteration also yields tick=0, color=1 → R=1,G=0,B=0. Startup state matches.

led1 output is *io_0 = tick%2 where tick=millis()/2000. tick=0 → LOW (off) for 0–2s, tick=1 → HIGH (on) 2–4s, tick=2 → LOW 4–6s, etc. This gives 2s on / 2s off indefinitely. Note startup is off, but the requirement only specifies 2s on/2s off interval, which holds.
colors[]={1,2,4,3,6,5,7}; tick%7==0 → color=1 → R=1,G=0,B=0. All three RGBs share the same color bits via io_1/4/7, io_2/5/8, io_3/6/9, so all display Red synchronously.
tick%7==1 → color=2 → R=0,G=1,B=0 = Green on all three RGBs synchronously.
tick%7==2 → color=4 → R=0,G=0,B=1 = Blue on all three RGBs synchronously.
tick%7==3 → color=3 → R=1,G=1,B=0 = Yellow on all three RGBs synchronously.
tick%7==4 → color=6 → R=0,G=1,B=1 = Cyan on all three RGBs synchronously.
tick%7==5 → color=5 → R=1,G=0,B=1 = Magenta on all three RGBs synchronously.
tick%7==6 → color=7 → R=1,G=1,B=1 = White on all three RGBs synchronously.
color index = (millis()/2000)%7, so each color is held for exactly 2000ms before the next. The loop's 10ms gate does not affect the 2s boundaries materially.
tick%7 wraps from 6 (White) back to 0 (Red) at the next 2s boundary, restarting the sequence.
Both led1 (tick%2) and RGB color (tick%7) are derived from the same millis()/2000 tick in the same loop iteration, so they update simultaneously and independently (different moduli).
setup() writes hw_value_io_0/1/2 which are initialized false, so pins 2,3,4 are LOW at power-on; all three LEDs off. Satisfies.
hw_value_io_3 initialized true, so setup writes pin 5 (rgb R) HIGH while G/B (pins 6,7) are LOW from false defaults; common cathode RGB shows red. Satisfies.
hw_value_io_6/7 initialized 0; setup attaches servos and writes command 0 (previous -1 differs), so both servos at 0 degrees. Satisfies.
angle formula: phase 0-2000 ramps 0->180, 2000-4000 holds 180, 4000-6000 ramps 180->0, 6000-8000 holds 0. Both servos get same angle. Sweeps 0->180->0. Satisfies.
Ramp from 0 to 180 spans phase 0..2000 = 2000ms, and 180 to 0 spans 4000..6000 = 2000ms. Each sweep takes 2 seconds. Satisfies.
Phase 6000-8000 holds angle 0 for 2000ms before next cycle ramp begins at phase 0. Pause at 0 degrees is 2 seconds. Satisfies.
Phase 2000-4000 holds angle 180 for 2000ms. Pause at 180 degrees is 2 seconds. Satisfies.
phase=now%8000 and endpoints derived from now repeat every 8000ms indefinitely; loop keeps calling ProgramPage1. Sequence repeats infinitely. Satisfies.

LED outputs are gated by endpoints && next==k, where endpoints=(now+2000)/4000 increments at phase 2000 and 6000 (the 180 and 0 endpoints). next=(endpoints+2)%3 cycles 0,1,2, so each endpoint turns on the next LED in sequence. Satisfies.
endpoints increments indefinitely and next cycles mod 3, so LED sequence repeats infinitely. Satisfies.
rgb=endpoints%3 changes at each endpoint (phase 2000 and 6000), cycling 0,1,2 -> red, green, blue. Satisfies.
Both LED and RGB outputs derive from the same endpoints counter, so they change at the same endpoint moments. Synchronized. Satisfies.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which sets sysml_state_ledOn=false, but setup writes pin 2 from hw_value_io_0 which is the static initializer false, so pin 2 is LOW at power-on. However the first loop() call runs ProgramPage1 with elapsed 0, leaving ledOn false, so pin 2 stays LOW. LED off at power-on is satisfied.

At power-on colorIndex=0. setup writes pins 3-8 from hw_value_io_1..6 which are static 0, so all RGB channels are 0 (off), not red. The first loop() call computes colorIndex 0 -> R=255,G=0,B=0 and writes red, but that is after setup, not at power-on/reset. Initialization state is not red.
ledAccumMs accumulates elapsed ms; at >=2000 it subtracts 2000 and toggles ledOn. With 10ms loop gating, toggles occur every ~2000ms, giving a 2-second blink interval.

colorIndex increments every 2000ms and wraps at 7. The RGB mapping: index0 R=255,G=0,B=0 red; index1 R=0,G=255,B=0 green; index2 R=0,G=0,B=255 blue; index3 R=255,G=255,B=0 yellow; index4 R=0,G=255,B=255 cyan; index5 R=255,G=0,B=255 magenta; index6 (else) R=255,G=255,B=255 white. Sequence and 2s each satisfied.
servo1PosDeg init 0; on servo tick, if ==0 set to 180. Servo1 scans 0->180.
Else branch of servo1 sets 180->0.
servo2 init 180; if ==180 set to 0.
Else branch sets servo2 0->180.
servo3 init 90; if ==90 set to 135.
Else branch sets servo3 135->90.
servoAccumMs accumulates elapsed and toggles all servos at >=2000ms, giving 2-second scan interval.
All three accumulators use the same io_10 elapsed and 2000ms thresholds, so LED, color, and servo transitions occur together each 2s and repeat continuously via loop().
loop() reads A3 and A4 every 5ms, calls ProgramPage1, and writes all LED pins each iteration, so LED states track potentiometer values continuously.
io_0 (pot1/A3) is scaled by 255/1023 into io_2, which drives pin 2 (led1) via analogWrite.
io_1 (pot2/A4) is scaled by 255/1023 into io_3, which drives pin 3 (led2) via analogWrite.
io_4 is true only when both io_0 and io_1 equal 1023, and pin 4 (led3) is driven HIGH in that case.
rgb1 red (pin5) and rgb2 red (pin8) use io_0 scaled to 0-255; green (pins 6,9) use io_1 scaled to 0-255.
When both pots are 1023, io_7 and io_10 are set to 255; red and green are also 255, so both RGB LEDs show white.
Both RGB LEDs receive identical computed values (io_5/6/7 and io_8/9/10 from same formulas) and are rewritten every loop iteration.
analogRead yields 0-1023; brightness and RGB components are scaled by 255/1023 (and sum/2046 for blue), producing 0-255 values.
setup() writes hw_value_io_0 which is initialized false, so digitalWrite(2, LOW) turns led1 off at startup before any loop update.
io_0 = tick%2 where tick=millis()/2000, so pin 2 is LOW for the first 2s then HIGH for 2s, alternating indefinitely. 2s on, 2s off.
colors[]={1,2,4,3,6,5,7} indexed by tick%7 gives R,G,B,Y,C,M,W in order and repeats.
tick increments every 2000ms and rgb index changes each tick, so each color lasts 2 seconds.
io_4 = tick%100 starts at 0 (00) and increments each 2s tick.
tick%100 wraps from 99 to 0 at the next 2s tick, resetting to 00 and continuing.

hw_shift595_io_4 sends units digit (value/1%10) first then tens digit (value/10%10). With two cascaded 595s, first shiftOut goes to sr1 (sevseg1) and second to sr2 (sevseg2). So sevseg1 gets units and sevseg2 gets tens — reversed from requirement.
shiftOut on A0/A2 with A1 latch sends segment data to the 595 chain; digits table maps values to segment patterns. Data is sent to shift registers.

All outputs derive from tick=millis()/2000, so LED, RGB, and displays all change on 2s boundaries. However the display only updates when io_4 changes (every 2s), and LED/RGB also every 2s — timing is 2s for all.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init (resets state) then writes hw_value_io_0=99 to shift registers via hw_shift595_io_0, producing digits[9]=0x6f for both digits ("99"). LED pins 2,3,4 and RGB pins 5-10 are written LOW from hw_value_io_1..9 which are all false at startup, so all LEDs off. Matches requirement.
ProgramPage1 computes digit=9-phase with phase=step%10 and step=millis()/2000. At step 0 digit=9, so the first displayed countdown value is 9. The countdown begins at 9.
step increments every 2000ms via millis()/2000, and digit=9-phase decrements by 1 each step (phase increments by 1). So the countdown value decrements by 1 every 2 seconds.
io_0=digit*11 produces e.g. digit 8 -> 88, digit 7 -> 77, and hw_shift595_io_0 renders both digits from value/1%10 and value/10%10, so displays show the doubled countdown value. Matches requirement.

Single-color LEDs are driven by io_1,io_2,io_3 = active && color==0/1/2. color cycles 0,1,2 each step (2s), so led1,led2,led3 light in sequence each staying 2s. However active requires step!=0 && digit!=0, so during the first step (digit 9, step 0) no LED is on, and at digit 0 all off. The sequence still cycles led1->led2->led3 each 2s during countdown. Matches.
RGB channels io_4/io_7 (red), io_5/io_8 (green), io_6/io_9 (blue) are set from color==0/1/2, and color changes each 2s step. So rgb1 and rgb2 cycle red, green, blue every 2 seconds. Matches.

When digit==0 (step 9), io_0=0 so displays show "00"; io_1..io_3 = active && ... with active false (digit==0), so all single LEDs off; io_4..io_9 = digit==0 || ... = true, so all RGB channels on = white. Matches.
phase=step%10 wraps at step 10 back to 0, so digit returns to 9 and the countdown restarts from 9 automatically. The system restarts the countdown from 9 after reaching 0. Matches.
ProgramPage1_Init sets led1State and led2State to false; setup writes hw_value_io_0/io_1 (both false) to pins 2 and 3 as LOW, so both LEDs are off at power-on.

Buttons are wired to GND with INPUT_PULLUP, so pressed reads LOW; code treats HIGH as pressed (io_2 = digitalRead(4)==HIGH), inverting the button semantics. A physical press yields io_2=false, so stableBtn1 never becomes true and led1 never toggles.

Hold timer is set to 2000 on toggle and decremented by elapsed ms, but the toggle path is unreachable because button polarity is inverted (pressed reads LOW, code requires HIGH). No toggle occurs, so no 2s stability window is produced.
Same inverted polarity on pin 5: pressed reads LOW but code requires HIGH, so stableBtn2 never asserts and led2 never toggles.
holdBtn2RemainingMs=2000 is set only in the toggle branch, which is unreachable due to inverted btn2 polarity; no 2s stability after a btn2 toggle is produced.
btn3 on pin 6 also uses inverted polarity (pressed reads LOW, code requires HIGH), so the reset branch that sets both LED states false is never entered by a physical press.
holdBtn3RemainingMs=2000 is set only in the btn3 reset branch, which is unreachable because btn3 polarity is inverted; no 2s off-state hold after reset occurs.

Debounce logic exists (accumulate while pressed, stable at >=20ms, reset to 0 when released), but the pressed condition is inverted relative to the pullup wiring, so the debounce operates on the wrong signal and does not debounce actual presses.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init, Serial.begin(9600), pinMode(2,INPUT_PULLUP), TM1637Display constructed with CLK=4/DIO=5 and setBrightness, and hw_dht_0.begin() on pin 7; loop polls serial, button, and DHT, so the system enters a state receiving serial and button input.
TEMP parses to mode 3; humidity is false for mode 3, so io_4 = (int32_t)io_1 (temperature) when DHT valid, and the display shows that value.
HUMI parses to mode 2; humidity is true for mode 2, so io_4 = (int32_t)io_2 (humidity) when DHT valid, and the display shows it.
BOTH parses to mode 1; humidity alternates every 2000ms via (now-changed)/2000%2, so io_4 alternates between temperature and humidity, and the display updates on each change.

Button D2 is debounced and passed as io_0; on a rising edge (press) sysml_state_serialEnabled toggles, and that flag gates the periodic serial output trigger, so pressing toggles serial output on/off.
setup() initializes all hw_value_* statics to false and writes LOW to every output pin (2-9,10-13,44,45) before loop runs, so all LEDs and bar segments are off at reset.
At stage 1, first=true, second=false, so io_0 (pin2/led1)=HIGH and io_1 (pin3/led2)=LOW. led1 on, led2 off.
rgb1 R=pin4=io_2, G=pin5=io_3, B=pin6=io_4. At stage1 io_2=stage==1 true, io_3=io_4=stage==3 false. R on, G/B off = red.
Segments 0-2 map to pins 10,11,12 (A1-A3) and equal first, which is true at stage1; segments 3-5 (A4-A6) equal second=false. First three on.
stage derived from millis()/2000: tick 0 -> stage0 (0-2s), tick1 -> stage1 (2-4s), tick2 -> stage2 (4-6s), tick3 -> stage3 (6-8s). Stage1 spans 2s.
At stage2, first=false, second=true: io_0 (led1)=LOW, io_1 (led2)=HIGH. led2 on, led1 off.
rgb2 R=pin7=io_5, G=pin8=io_6, B=pin9=io_7. At stage2 io_5=false, io_6=second=true, io_7=stage==3 false. G on only = green.
Segments 3-5 (pins 13,44,45 = A4-A6) equal second, true at stage2; segments 0-2 equal first=false. Last three on.
Stage2 occupies tick2, i.e. 4-6s, a 2-second window.
At stage3, first=true and second=true, so io_0 (led1) and io_1 (led2) both HIGH.
At stage3 io_3=io_4=true (rgb1 G,B on, R off) and io_6=true, io_7=true (rgb2 G,B on, R off). Both cyan.
At stage3 first=true and second=true, so all six segment outputs are HIGH.
Stage3 occupies tick3, i.e. 6-8s, a 2-second window.
(tick-1)%3+1 cycles 1,2,3,1,2,3... indefinitely as millis grows, repeating states 1-3.
ProgramPage1_Init sets all three brightness globals to 0.0, and setup() writes those zero values to pins 2/3/4 via analogWrite before any loop iteration, so all LEDs start off.
On a rising edge of btn1 (io_3 true, previous false), led1Brightness = io_6*255/1023 where io_6 is analogRead(A3) (pot1, 0-1023), giving 0-255; loop writes it to pin 2.
On a rising edge of btn2 (io_4), led2Brightness = io_7*255/1023 with io_7 from analogRead(A4) (pot2), and loop writes it to pin 3.
On a rising edge of btn3 (io_5), led3Brightness = io_8*255/1023 with io_8 from analogRead(A5) (pot3), and loop writes it to pin 4.

The stableTimer==0 branch clears all brightnesses every 201 steps (since stableTimer increments each step and is never reset), so a set brightness is wiped roughly every 201 loop steps (~2.01s at 10ms), not held for at least 2s after the press; the press occurs at an arbitrary phase within the cycle, so the LED can be cleared well before 2s elapse.
With no button pressed, the stableTimer==0 branch still zeroes all three brightnesses every 201 steps, so LEDs do not maintain their current levels; they are periodically forced off.
The rising-edge assignments are per-button and only touch their own brightness variable, so pressing btn1 changes only led1Brightness; the other LEDs' values are untouched by that press.

ProgramPage1_Init sets mode=0, servo angles 0.0, ledOn false; setup attaches servos and writes hw_value_io_0/io_1 (both 0) and digitalWrite(2, LOW) since hw_value_io_2 is false. First loop iteration: mode==0, no pending, so io_0=0, io_1=0, io_2=false; servos written 0 and LED LOW. Initial state matches.

On btn1 press (io_3 true, previous false), first=true, pending=1. mode==0 so event applied: mode=1, began=millis(). Outputs: io_0=90, io_1=0, io_2=true (mode==1). Servo1 written 90, LED HIGH. Matches.
On btn2 press from mode 0, second=true, pending=2, mode==0 so event applied: mode=2, began=millis(). Outputs: io_0=0, io_1=180, io_2=false (mode!=1 and mode!=3). Servo2 written 180, LED LOW. Matches.

From mode 1, btn2 press: second=true, pending=2. Condition (mode==1&&event==2) makes mode=3, began=millis(). Outputs: io_0=0, io_1=0, io_2=(millis()-began)%4000<2000. At began, (0)%4000=0<2000 so LED HIGH for first 2s, then LOW for 2s, period 4s = 0.25 Hz. Both servos return to 0. Matches.

In mode 3, subsequent button presses are gated by (mode==0 || elapsed>=2000). After 2s, a new press sets pending and event applied: mode=event (1 or 2) since mode==3 not in the transition conditions, so mode becomes 1 or 2. Before 2s, presses are ignored (pending retained but not applied until 2s elapse). So state maintained until a button press after 2s. Requirement says maintained until btn1 or btn2 pressed again; the 2s gate delays but does not violate 'until pressed again' since presses within 2s are ignored. Matches.
In mode 1, began set at press. Outputs io_0=90, io_2=true persist. New events gated until elapsed>=2000. So state held at least 2s. Matches.
In mode 2, began set at press. Outputs io_1=180, io_2=false persist. New events gated until elapsed>=2000. So state held at least 2s. Matches.
ProgramPage1_Init sets servoAngle=90 and movingLed=false; setup writes pin2 LOW (LED off) and writes servo command 90 since hw_servo_previous_io_3=-1. Initial state matches requirement.
On btn1 rising edge (up true) and target<180, next=target+30, so target increments by 30 up to 180. At target=180 the guard target<180 blocks further increment.
When next!=target, moving=true and began=millis(); io_0=moving drives pin2 HIGH (LED on). After elapsed>=2000, moving=false and current=target, so LED turns off once servo reaches new angle.
On btn2 rising edge (down true) and target>0, next=target-30, decrementing by 30 down to 0. At target=0 the guard target>0 blocks further decrement.
Same movement path as R003: next!=target sets moving=true, LED on via io_0, and after 2000ms moving=false, LED off. Applies to btn2 decrement.
At target=180, up with target<180 false so next==target, no movement, moving stays false, LED off. At target=0, down with target>0 false, same. No effect and LED remains off.
Movement interpolates current=start+(target-start)*elapsed/2000.0 over 2000ms, giving smooth motion; moving stays true until elapsed>=2000, so LED remains on for 2000ms (at least 2 seconds).

setup() writes the initial static values: hw_value_io_0/io_1 are 0 so analogWrite(2/3,0) gives 0% duty (LEDs off), and all hw_value_io_2_segment_* are false so digitalWrite(4..13,LOW) keeps all bar segments off. No earlier write turns anything on before these.

loop reads A3 into hw_value_io_3, ProgramPage1 computes *io_0=io_3*255.0/1023.0 (uniform 0..255 for ADC 0..1023), and loop writes that to pin 2 via analogWrite. Pin 2 is led1:A per wiring, so pot1 controls led1 brightness.

loop reads A4 into hw_value_io_4, ProgramPage1 computes *io_1=io_4*255.0/1023.0, and loop writes it to pin 3 via analogWrite. Pin 3 is led2:A, so pot2 controls led2 brightness with uniform 0..255 mapping.

loop reads A5 into hw_value_io_5; count=(int)(io_5*10.0/1023.0) yields 0..10 (10 only at ADC 1023). Segments are set count>0..count>9, so count=0 lights none and count=10 lights all ten (pins 4..13 = A1..A10). Uniform mapping and endpoints satisfied.
loop runs continuously, re-reads all three pots every 5ms, recomputes outputs via ProgramPage1, and rewrites pins 2,3 and 4..13 each pass, so brightness and segment count track current pot values.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init setting displayNumber=0 and brightnesses=0, then hw_shift595_io_0(0) shifts digits[0]=0x3f for both digits (tens and units both 0), and analogWrite(2,0)/analogWrite(3,0) leave both LEDs off. Displays show "00" and LEDs off at reset.

When displayNumber is even, brightnessLed1 = io_3*255/1023 (io_3 = analogRead(A3) from pot1), then analogWrite(2, ...) drives led1. Mapping to 0-255 is present. However when the number is odd, led1 is forced to 0 regardless of pot1, which is the required even/odd indication behavior, so pot1 brightness control applies only in even state. The mapping and PWM output path exist.
When displayNumber is odd, brightnessLed2 = io_4*255/1023 (io_4 = analogRead(A4) from pot2), then analogWrite(3,...) drives led2. Mapping to 0-255 present.

displayNumber = floor(io_5*99/1023) via truncation with conditional subtract, giving 0-99 from pot3 (A5). hw_shift595_io_0 writes units digit (value/1%10) first then tens digit (value/10%10) into the two chained shift registers; sr1 feeds sevseg1 and sr2 feeds sevseg2. Need to verify digit ordering: first shiftOut goes to sr1 (sevseg1) but uses units digit, second goes to sr2 (sevseg2) using tens digit — this is reversed from the requirement (tens on sevseg1, units on sevseg2).
When displayNumber is even (displayNumber == 2*floor(displayNumber/2)), brightnessLed1 = io_3*255/1023 (nonzero for pot1>0) and brightnessLed2 = 0.0, so led1 on and led2 off. Matches requirement.
When displayNumber is odd, the even test fails so brightnessLed1 = 0.0 and brightnessLed2 = io_4*255/1023, giving led1 off and led2 on. Matches requirement.
loop() runs every 5ms, re-reads A3/A4/A5, calls ProgramPage1, updates shift registers when displayNumber changes and always analogWrites both LEDs. Continuous update implemented.

setup() writes pin2 HIGH (led1 on), pin6 LOW (led2 off), pin3 HIGH (rgb R on), pin4 LOW (G off), pin5 LOW (B off) via initial hw_value_io_0=true, io_1=false, io_2=true, io_3=false, io_4=false. This yields red on led1 and rgb1 red, led2 off at power-on.
red = millis()/2000%2==0. From t=0 to t=1999 red=true: pin2 HIGH, pin6 LOW, pin3 HIGH, pin4 LOW, pin5 LOW → led1 on, led2 off, rgb red. Duration is 2000ms.
At t=2000 red=false: pin2 LOW (led1 off), pin6 HIGH (led2 on), pin3 LOW, pin4 LOW, pin5 HIGH → rgb blue. Lasts until t=3999, i.e. 2000ms.
The millis()/2000%2 expression alternates every 2000ms indefinitely; loop() continuously re-evaluates and writes outputs, so the two states repeat forever.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which sets timerSeconds=0, but hw_value_io_1 is a static initialized to -1 and is never reset in setup. The setup block then calls hw_shift595_io_1(-1) since -1 != INT32_MIN, which writes segments=0 (all off) to the shift register. So the display is off at power-on. However, note the display is off because value -1 is invalid, giving segments=0. This satisfies the requirement.

The loop gates on hw_elapsed < 10UL, so it runs every 10ms, not every 1000ms. ProgramPage1 computes seconds=millis()/1000 and io_1=(seconds*2)%10. The timer value is derived from millis()/1000*2, which does increment by 2 per real second. But the loop runs every 10ms and recomputes from millis, so the displayed value changes every second by 2. The increment-by-2-per-second behavior is implemented via (seconds*2)%10. This matches the requirement.

The loop recomputes io_1 each iteration and calls hw_shift595_io_1 when the value changes, updating the display. The display updates to the current timer value (mod 10). This satisfies the update requirement.
io_1=(seconds*2)%10 already reduces to last digit. For timer=12, seconds=6, (6*2)%10=2, displays '2'. The %10 ensures only last digit. This matches the example.
The loop continues indefinitely, recomputing from millis each iteration, so the timer keeps incrementing and display keeps updating following the rules. This satisfies continuation.
setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which zeroes counters, and hw_value_io_* statics default false; all digitalWrite calls in setup write LOW, so bar graph pins 5-13,44 and LEDs 2,3 start LOW (off).
On a stable press (stable && raw), ++sysml_state_currentCounter increments by exactly 1; overflow branch only triggers when >10.
Outputs io_1..io_10 = currentCounter>0..>9, so counter 1 lights 1 segment, counter 10 lights all 10; mapped to pins 5-13 and 44 (A1-A10).
When increment makes counter 11 (>10), counter set to 0 and overflowCounter incremented mod 4.
overflowCounter 0: io_11=(0&1)!=0 false, io_12=(0&2)!=0 false, both LEDs LOW = 00.
overflowCounter 1: io_11 true (bit0), io_12 false (bit1) => led1 on, led2 off = 01.
overflowCounter 2: io_11 false, io_12 true => 10.
overflowCounter 3: both bits set => 11; next overflow (3+1)%4=0 wraps to 00.
Raw input change resets changed=millis(); stable only updates after >=150ms of unchanged raw, and counter increments only on stable rising edge.
Outputs are recomputed each loop from persistent counters; no other code changes counters, so state holds until next debounced press.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which sets sysml_state_ledOn=false, then pinMode(2,OUTPUT) and digitalWrite(2, hw_value_io_0 ? HIGH : LOW) with hw_value_io_0 initialized false, so pin 2 is driven LOW at reset, LED off.
ProgramPage1 computes phase=millis()%9000 and sets io_0 true when phase<1000, so from phase 0 to 999 the LED is HIGH for 1 second.
For phase in [1000,3000) the expression is false, so the LED is LOW for 2000 ms (2 seconds).
For phase in [3000,6000) the second clause is true, so the LED is HIGH for 3000 ms (3 seconds).
For phase in [6000,9000) both clauses are false, so the LED is LOW for 3000 ms (3 seconds).
The modulo 9000 wraps phase back to 0 after 9000 ms, and loop() runs continuously, so the four-step sequence repeats indefinitely.
setup() attaches servo and writes hw_value_io_3, which is initialized to 0 and never changed before setup, so command=0 is written at startup. Satisfies default 0 degrees.
io_0 is analogRead(A3) (pot1). minimum=(int)(io_0*90.0/1023.0) maps 0..1023 to 0..90. Satisfies.
io_1 is analogRead(A4) (pot2). maximum=90+(int)(io_1*90.0/1023.0) maps 0..1023 to 90..180. Satisfies.
io_2 is analogRead(A5) (pot3). Output = minimum + io_2*(maximum-minimum)/1023.0, mapping pot3 0..1023 to [minimum, maximum]. Satisfies.
loop() runs continuously, samples all three pots every 10ms, recomputes ProgramPage1, and writes servo when command changes. Satisfies continuous update.
setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which sets modeManual=true, and writes analogWrite(2, hw_value_io_0) where hw_value_io_0 is initialized to 0, so LED is off and Manual Mode is the start state.
In Manual Mode io_3 (A3/pot1) is mapped: 0->0, >=1023->255, else io_3*255/1023, and written to pin 2 via analogWrite.
In the Manual branch only io_3 is used; io_4 and io_5 (pot2/pot3) are not referenced in that branch, so they are ignored.
When modeManual and stableBtn1Pressed rising edge, modeManual is set false (Auto). Debounced stable button drives this.
In Auto Mode, io_4 (pot2) is used as minimum and io_5 (pot3) as maximum in the interpolation; at endpoints it outputs min/max values.
transitionElapsed accumulates io_6 (ms) and interpolation uses transitionElapsed/2000, so each transition spans 2000 ms; toggles toMax at 2000.
When not modeManual and stableBtn2Pressed rising edge, modeManual set true (Manual).
Debounce counters set to 150 on press edge and decremented by elapsed ms; stable state updated when counter reaches <=0.

No minimum 2-second dwell is enforced before mode switching; a btn1 press immediately after entering Manual (or btn2 after Auto) switches mode regardless of elapsed time. The 2000ms logic only governs auto brightness phase, not mode persistence.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which sets ledCount=0, but the LED output variables hw_value_io_0/1/2 are static-initialized false and never set from ledCount; digitalWrite(2/3/4, LOW) turns all LEDs off. hw_value_io_3 is 0, and setup calls hw_shift595_io_3(0) which writes digits[0]=0x3f inverted to 0xC0, displaying '0'. Both conditions satisfied.

In ProgramPage1, leds is only updated inside the 2000ms branch via xorshift from randomState, giving leds=randomState&7 (0-3 LEDs). However, the first update occurs at the first loop iteration because last=0 and now>=2000 is false initially... actually now-last>=2000 requires now>=2000, so first selection at ~2000ms. The selection is random via xorshift seeded from analogRead. This satisfies random 0-3 LEDs every 2 seconds.

io_3 is computed as sum of the three LED booleans each call, and loop writes it to the shift register whenever it changes (hw_value_io_3 != previous). So the display updates in the same loop iteration the LEDs change. Satisfies immediate update.

loop() runs indefinitely; the 2000ms branch in ProgramPage1 re-fires each time now-last>=2000, updating leds and thus LEDs and display every 2 seconds. No termination. Satisfies indefinite repetition.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which sets colorIndex=0, then analogWrite(2/3/4) with hw_value_io_0/1/2 all initialized to 0, so all three channels are 0 (off) at power-on. Common cathode wiring means 0 = off.
First press: io_3 true, previousPressed false, so colorIndex=(0+1)%4=1. Then io_0=255 (red), io_1=0, io_2=0. analogWrite(2,255) drives red on, green/blue off.
Second press: colorIndex=(1+1)%4=2, io_1=255, io_0=0, io_2=0, so green on, red/blue off.
Third press: colorIndex=(2+1)%4=3, io_2=255, io_0=0, io_1=0, so blue on, red/green off.
Fourth press: colorIndex=(3+1)%4=0, all three outputs 0, so LED off.
Modulo 4 wraps colorIndex back to 0 after fourth press, so fifth press gives 1 (red), sixth 2 (green), seventh 3 (blue), eighth 0 (off), repeating the sequence.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which sets digit=0, but hw_value_io_2 stays 0 and hw_shift595_previous_io_2 is INT32_MIN, so hw_shift595_io_2(0) runs in setup. digits[0]=0x3f, bits inverted to 0xC0, shiftOut MSBFIRST sends 0xC0. Q0..Q6 map to segments A..G; 0xC0 has bits 6,7 set, so Q6=1 (segment G on) and Q0..Q5=0 (A-F off). That displays only the middle bar, not "0".
At startup digit=0, so sysml_value_3..12 are all (digit>=1..9)=false; setup writes LOW to pins 4-13. Bar graph is fully off.

Init sets parityEven=true, so io_0=true, io_1=false. But setup writes digitalWrite(2, hw_value_io_0 ? HIGH : LOW) with hw_value_io_0 still false (ProgramPage1 not yet called), and digitalWrite(3,...) with hw_value_io_1 false. Both LEDs off at startup.
Accumulator adds elapsed ms each loop; when >=2000 subtracts 2000 and increments digit, wrapping 9→0. Loop runs every ~5ms so increments occur roughly every 2s. Digit cycles 0..9 then 0.

hw_shift595_io_2 is called when digit changes and writes the digit pattern via shiftOut. However the bit inversion (bits=~bits) combined with the wiring Q0..Q6→A..G means the displayed pattern is the complement of the intended digit, so the display does not show the current number correctly.
Segments are (digit>=1)..(digit>=9) mapped to pins 4..12, so digit N lights N segments A1..AN. For 3, segments 0,1,2 true → pins 4,5,6 (A1-A3) HIGH. Matches requirement.
parityEven computed as digit==2*floor(digit/2). For even digit, parityEven=true → io_0=true (led1 on), io_1=!parityEven=false (led2 off). Matches.
For odd digit, parityEven=false → io_0=false (led1 off), io_1=true (led2 on). Matches.
Accumulator adds actual elapsed ms and subtracts 2000 on trigger, so period is ~2000ms plus loop granularity (~5ms). Not exactly 2 seconds; there is drift/overshoot of up to ~5ms per cycle.

On a digit change, ProgramPage1 updates all outputs, then loop writes LEDs, shift register, and bar graph sequentially in the same iteration. All update within the same loop pass (microseconds apart), effectively simultaneous.
hw_shift595_io_2 uses shiftOut(A0,A2,MSBFIRST,...) with A1 latch, driving sr1 which connects to sevseg1. Shift register drives the display.
Bar graph segments written directly via digitalWrite on pins 4-13, no shift register. Matches.
led1 (pin 2) and led2 (pin 3) driven from parityEven and its complement, indicating parity. Both used.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which sets count=0, then hw_value_io_0 is 0 and differs from INT32_MIN, so hw_shift595_io_0(0) runs. For value 0, units digit digits[0]=0x3f, tens digit digits[0]=0x3f, both shifted out inverted. Both displays show '0', i.e. "00".
On a rising edge of the button (io_1 true, previousPressed false), count+37 is computed; if <=99 it becomes the new count. E.g. 0->37, 37->74. Increment by 37 is implemented.

hw_shift595_io_0 shifts the units digit (value/1%10) first into sr1, then the tens digit (value/10%10) into sr2 via daisy chain. sr1 drives sevseg1 and sr2 drives sevseg2, so sevseg1 gets tens and sevseg2 gets units.
When count+37 > 99, conditional is set to 0, so count resets to 0 and displays show "00". E.g. 74+37=111>99 -> 0.

After ProgramPage1 updates count, loop compares hw_value_io_0 to previous and calls hw_shift595_io_0 immediately, shifting new digits out and latching with A1 HIGH. Display updates in the same loop iteration as the press.

At reset ProgramPage1_Init sets mode=1 but the local static mode in ProgramPage1 is 0, so on first loop all io_1..io_3 are false and all RGB values 0; setup writes LOW/0 to pins 2,3,4 and analogWrite 0 to RGB pins, so all LEDs are off at power-on.

First press: mode 0->1 (Mode 1). Second press after 2s: mode 1->2, then rainbow branch computes values from rainbow[]={3,6,5} (bits: 3=011 yellow, 6=110 cyan, 5=101 purple) with interpolation, so Mode 2 shows yellow/cyan/purple.
Third press: mode 2->3; mode==3 sets every RGB channel to 192 (equal R=G=B warm white), and io_3=mode==3 drives led3 HIGH while led1/led2 are LOW.
Fourth press: mode 3->0; mode 0 matches no branch so all RGB values stay 0 and io_1..io_3 are all false, turning all single-color LEDs off and keeping them off.
Fifth press: mode 0->1; mode==1 sets channel==led to 255, giving rgb1 red, rgb2 green, rgb3 blue, and io_1=mode==1 turns led1 on while led2/led3 off.
The press condition requires !started || (now-changed)>=2000, so a press within 2s of the last mode change does not increment mode; mode is maintained.
In mode 2 the value interpolates linearly from current rainbow color to next over each 1000ms window using (time%1000)/1000.0, producing smooth transitions between yellow, cyan, and purple.

Single-color LEDs are driven by io_1..io_3 which are true only for modes 1 and 3 respectively; mode 2 and mode 4 leave all single-color LEDs off, matching the described indication (led1 for Mode 1, led3 for Mode 3, off for Modes 2 and 4).
setup() initializes all hw_value_io_* to false and writes LOW to pins 2-12 before any loop iteration, so all LEDs in both bar graphs are off at power-on/reset.
During phase 1 (millis 2000-3999), step=0..9 gives index=0..9, lighting io_0..io_9 sequentially, which map to pins 2..11 = bargraph1 A1..A10.

bargraph2 pins 3..12 are driven by io_1..io_10. io_10 is hardcoded false, so bargraph2 LED1 (pin 3) is never lit; when bargraph1 reaches LED1 (index 0), io_1..io_10 are all false so bargraph2 is off, but for i>1 bargraph2 lights LED i-1 via io_{i-1}. The i=1 case is satisfied; the general i-1 mapping holds for i>=2. However io_10=false means bargraph2 LED10 never lights, but that corresponds to i=11 which doesn't occur. So the mapping is satisfied.

For phase 2 (millis 4000-5999), step=10..17 gives index=18-step=8..1, then next cycle step 0..9 again. Wait: step=10→index=8, step=17→index=1. So it goes 8,7,...,1 then wraps to 0,1,...9. The right-to-left phase starts at index 8, not 9 (LED10), and never reaches index 9 in the descending phase. LED10 (index 9) is only lit at end of ascending phase. So descending starts at LED9, not LED10.
Right-to-left phase begins at index 8 (LED9), not LED10, and descends to index 1 then jumps to 0. It does not start with LED10.
During descending phase index goes 8..1, io_1..io_8 light bargraph2 LEDs 1..8 (i-1 mapping), and at index 0 all off. Mapping holds for i>=2; at i=1 bargraph2 off. Satisfied.
phase=millis()/2000UL, so each index step lasts 2000ms = 2 seconds.
phase increments indefinitely and step=(phase-1)%18 wraps, so the pattern repeats forever.
setup() calls hw_shift595_io_2(hw_value_io_2) with hw_value_io_2 initialized to 0, so digits[0]=0x3f is shifted out at power-on, displaying '0'.
pot1 on A3 is read into io_0 and mapped via (int)(io_0*9.0/1023.0), giving 0..9 for input 0..1023.
pot2 on A4 is read into io_1 and mapped via (int)(io_1*9.0/1023.0), giving 0..9.
The two mapped values are summed in the expression (int)(io_0*9/1023)+(int)(io_1*9/1023).
The sum is taken modulo 10, so sums above 9 yield the last digit (e.g., 12→2, 15→5).
loop() re-reads both analog inputs every 5ms and recomputes/updates the display when the value changes, continuously tracking the pots.

setup() calls hw_shift595_io_1(hw_value_io_1) with hw_value_io_1 initialized to 0, so both digits are written as digit 0 (0x3f inverted). The value 0 is valid, so digits[0] is used for both units and tens, displaying "00" at power-on.
ProgramPage1 computes io_1 = io_0*99.0/1023.0 with io_0 from analogRead(A3) in 0..1023, yielding 0..99. The mapping is implemented.

hw_shift595_io_1 shifts units digit first (value/1%10) then tens digit (value/10%10). With two cascaded 595s, the first shiftOut ends in sr2 (units, sevseg2) and the second in sr1 (tens, sevseg1), matching the required assignment.
loop() re-reads A3 every 5ms, recomputes the mapped value, and re-shifts whenever the value changes, so the display tracks the potentiometer dynamically.

The mapping 0..1023 -> 0..99 cannot produce a value outside 0-99, so the out-of-range branch is unreachable. However the guard exists: valid = value>=0 && value<100, and when invalid segments=0 (all off). The requirement's condition is unattainable given the mapping, so the branch is never exercised; the code does implement a fallback but it shows blank, not "00". Since the condition cannot occur, this is not a reachable violation.

For pot values 0-127, all four range checks (128-255, 512-639, 640-767, 896-1023 for red; 256-383, 512-639, 768-895, 896-1023 for green; 384-511, 640-767, 768-895, 896-1023 for blue) evaluate false, so io_1/io_2/io_3 are all false and pins 2,3,4 are written LOW, turning all LEDs off.

For 128-255, red's first check (>=128 && <=255) is true so io_1=true; green's checks (256-383,512-639,768-895,896-1023) and blue's (384-511,640-767,768-895,896-1023) are all false, so only pin 2 is HIGH.

For 256-383, green's first check (>=256 && <=383) is true so io_2=true; red's checks (128-255,512-639,640-767,896-1023) and blue's (384-511,640-767,768-895,896-1023) are all false, so only pin 3 is HIGH.

For 384-511, blue's first check (>=384 && <=511) is true so io_3=true; red's checks (128-255,512-639,640-767,896-1023) and green's (256-383,512-639,768-895,896-1023) are all false, so only pin 4 is HIGH.

For 512-639, red's second check (>=512 && <=639) is true and green's second check (>=512 && <=639) is true, so io_1 and io_2 are true; blue's checks (384-511,640-767,768-895,896-1023) are all false, so pins 2 and 3 are HIGH.

For 640-767, red's third check (>=640 && <=767) is true and blue's second check (>=640 && <=767) is true, so io_1 and io_3 are true; green's checks (256-383,512-639,768-895,896-1023) are all false, so pins 2 and 4 are HIGH.

For 768-895, green's third check (>=768 && <=895) is true and blue's third check (>=768 && <=895) is true, so io_2 and io_3 are true; red's checks (128-255,512-639,640-767,896-1023) are all false, so pins 3 and 4 are HIGH.
For 896-1023, red's fourth check (>=896 && <=1023), green's fourth check, and blue's fourth check are all true, so io_1, io_2, io_3 are all true and pins 2,3,4 are HIGH.
loop() re-reads A3 every iteration (gated only by a 5ms sample interval), recomputes the range booleans, and writes all three pins each pass, so a new pot value updates the LED within ~5ms.
setup() attaches servos and writes hw_value_io_0/1/2, which are static-initialized to 0 and never changed before setup; each write(0) sets all servos to 0°.
All segment statics are false at startup, and setup writes LOW to pins 5-13 and 44, so all bargraph segments are off initially.
phase=millis()/2000%4; for t in [2000,4000) phase=1, io_0=180, io_1=io_2=0. Servo1 holds 180 for the full 2s window.
In phase 1, count=phase*3=3, so segments 0,1,2 (pins 5,6,7 = A1-A3) are HIGH and segments 3-9 LOW, held for the 2s phase.
In phase 2 (t in [4000,6000)), io_1=180 while io_0 stays 180 and io_2=0; servo2 holds 180 for 2s.
Phase 2 count=6, so segments 0-5 (A1-A6) HIGH and 6-9 LOW, held for the 2s phase.
In phase 3 (t in [6000,8000)), io_2=180 while io_0 and io_1 remain 180; servo3 holds 180 for 2s.
Phase 3 count=10, so all ten segments (A1-A10) are HIGH for the 2s phase.
At t=8000 phase wraps to 0, so io_0=io_1=io_2=0 in the same update; all three servos are written 0 in the same loop iteration.
At phase 0, count=0, so all segment booleans are false and all ten digitalWrite calls drive LOW in the same loop iteration.
Phase 0 spans t in [0,2000) and [8000,10000); after reset at 8000 the system stays in reset state for 2000ms before phase 1 at 10000.
Each phase occupies exactly a 2000ms window of millis()/2000%4, so state is maintained for 2s per phase.
Reset phase (phase 0) after phase 3 lasts from t=8000 to t=10000, i.e. 2000ms, satisfying the 2s reset persistence.

In displayPage 0 (default, reset to 0 on confirm), sysml_value_18 = (hours*100 + minutes) from sysml_state_clockMs, written to *io_6 and shown via showNumberDec. Clock advances each loop by io_8 elapsed ms. So the display shows current time when no reminder page is active.
hw_rx_parse accepts "TIME hhmm" producing 1*10000+payload; ProgramPage1 validates and sets sysml_state_clockMs = (hh*60+mm)*60000 and clockReady=true, so the RTC-simulated time is adopted.

items.reason: Three alarm variables alarmOne/Two/Three exist and are settable via SET1/SET2/SET3 serial commands (payload 2/3/4 prefix) which assign sysml_state_alarmOne/Two/Three in minutes. Defaults 420/720/1080.

evidence.text: sysml_state_alarmOne = ((((int32_t)(((double)(io_0 - ((((int32_t)(((double)io_0) / 10000)) - sysml_conditional_135) * 10000))) / 100)) - sysml_conditional_138) * 60) + ((io_0 - ((((int32_t)(((double)io_0) / 10000)) - sysml_conditional_139) * 10000)) - ((((int32_t)(((double)(io_0 - ((((int32_t)(((double)io_0) / 10000)) - sysml_conditional_140) * 10000))) / 100)) - sysml_conditional_143) * 100));

items.reason: When status==1, sysml_value_3/4/5 toggle true for age%1000<500, ORed into sysml_value_16, which sets tone command 2000 (buzzer) and LED io_5=true; otherwise 0/false. Confirm button (io_1) sets status to 2, ending the alarm. So intermittent buzzer and LED blink occur while waiting for confirmation.

When status==1 and age>=30000, status set to 3, batchMisses incremented; batchMisses added to missedCount and pendingWarnings; pendingWarnings>0 sets warningStep=true and decrements. warningStep output io_7 triggers Serial.println("missed dose"). So missed dose warning printed and missedCount accumulated.

previousPress (io_2/D3) and nextPress (io_3/D4) cycle displayPage 0..3; pages 1-3 show 1000+statusOne etc., i.e., today's reminder status. Confirm press resets page to 0. So buttons browse today's reminder status.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which resets modeOff/modeHold/colorIndex, but the phase accumulator in ProgramPage1 is a function-static initialized to 0 and never reset; on first loop call phase advances by dt and outputs red (io_0=255) for phase<2000, green for 2000-4000, blue for >=4000, cycling mod 6000. So on power-on red is shown first and each color lasts 2s. Satisfies startup cycling.
In cycling mode (hold=false, off=false) phase increments by dt mod 6000, and outputs map phase<2000→red, 2000-4000→green, >=4000→blue, each 2000ms. Cycling behavior implemented.
On rising edge of io_3 (k1), hold=true, which stops phase accumulation; outputs continue to reflect current phase, so the current color is held. Satisfies stop-and-hold.
When hold is set, phase stops updating and the output expressions still evaluate against the frozen phase, so the last displayed color remains. Satisfies Hold Mode.
On rising edge of io_4 (k2), hold=false and off=false; phase resumes from its frozen value, continuing cycling from where it stopped. Satisfies resume.
On rising edge of io_5 (k3), off=true; all three output expressions are gated by !off, so all channels become 0, turning the LED completely dark. Satisfies off.
With off=true all three analogWrite values are 0, so the RGB LED is fully off. Satisfies Off Mode.

Buttons are debounced with 25ms stability and sampled every 10ms; loop runs at ~10ms cadence, so state transitions occur within tens of milliseconds. Edge detection via previous[] ensures immediate response to presses. Satisfies immediate response.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which sets bit0/1/2 false, and hw_value_io_* globals are zero-initialized, so all digitalWrite calls in setup drive LOW. However the bar graph segments are wired to pins 8,9,10,11,12,13,44,45 (A1-A8 of bargraph), and the code drives those from io_6_segment_* which are all false at start, so all segments off. LEDs on pins 2,3,4 driven from io_0/1/2 false. All off at reset.
In ProgramPage1, on rising edge of button i, bits^=1<<i. For btn1 (i=0) this toggles bit0, and *io_0=bits&1 drives LED1 on pin 2. So each press toggles LED1 and lowest bit. Matches.

Segments are set by bits==N comparisons: segment_0=bits==1 ... segment_6=bits==7, segment_7=bits==8 (unreachable since bits is 3-bit). For value 5, segment_4=bits==5 drives pin 12. But the wiring maps bargraph A5 to mega pin 12, and the requirement says binary 101 lights segment 5 (PIN A5). Pin 12 is bargraph A5, so segment 5 lights. However the mapping is off-by-one relative to segment index naming but wiring matches: bits==5 -> io_6_segment_4 -> pin 12 -> A5. So value 5 lights A5. Correct. But value 0 lights nothing (no segment for 0), which is acceptable per '0-7'? Requirement says segment corresponding to value; value 0 has no segment. Ambiguous but example matches. Value 7 lights segment_6 -> pin 44 -> A7. Value 1 lights segment_0 -> pin 8 -> A1. So mapping value N -> pin (7+N) -> A(N). Matches A1-A7 for 1-7.

manual_debounce_input requires raw stable for >=150ms before updating stable[index], and forces stable=false when raw is false. A press shorter than 150ms never sets stable true, so ProgramPage1 never sees a rising edge and bits unchanged. Press ignored.
analogRead(A3)=0 gives hw_value_io_0=0; ProgramPage1 computes 0*180/1023=0; guard 0>=0&&0<=180 passes, command=(int)0=0, write(0) sets servo1 to 0°.
analogRead(A3)=1023 gives 1023*180/1023=180.0; guard 180<=180 passes, command=(int)180.0=180, write(180) sets servo1 to 180°.
Linear formula io_0*180/1023 maps the full 0..1023 ADC range proportionally to 0..180; intermediate values e.g. 512 -> 90.09 -> command 90, written when changed.
analogRead(A4)=0 gives io_1=0; both sysml_value_1 and sysml_value_2 compute 0; guards pass, commands 0 written to servo2 (pin3) and servo3 (pin4).
analogRead(A4)=1023 gives io_1=1023; both formulas yield 180.0; guards 180<=180 pass, commands 180 written to servo2 and servo3.
Both servo2 and servo3 use the identical expression io_1*180/1023 from the same A4 reading, so they track in unison proportionally across 0..180.
Loop samples pots every 5ms and writes only when the integer command changes, giving incremental smooth servo motion rather than jumps; no blocking delays.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init setting value=0, then hw_shift595_io_1(0) writes digits[0]=0x3f inverted to 0xC0 via shiftOut, and all bar graph pins 2-11 are written LOW since segment flags are false. Display shows 0, bar graph off.

loop accumulates elapsed ms into sysml_state_accumulatedMs; when >=2000 it subtracts 2000 and increments value (0->1->...->9->0). The 10ms gate and elapsed accumulation make increments occur every ~2s.
For value N, segment flags 0..N-1 are true (>=1..>=N), driving pins 2..(N+1) HIGH, i.e. N LEDs lit from A1 upward. Matches count equal to current number.
When value==9, conditional_0=0 so value resets to 0; all segment flags become false and pins 2-11 are written LOW, turning off all bar LEDs. Display also shows 0.

After ProgramPage1 updates value and flags, loop immediately calls hw_shift595_io_1 (on change) and digitalWrite for all bar pins in the same iteration, so both outputs reflect the new number without delay.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which sets angles to 0.0, but the servo write in setup uses hw_value_io_0/1/2 which are static-initialized to 0 and never updated before attach; write(0) is issued for each servo. LED pins are written from hw_value_io_3_segment_* which are false, so all LOW (off). Servos at 0 and LEDs off at init.

ProgramPage1 computes count from millis()/2000%20, count=step for step<=10, angle=count*18. At step 1 (t=2000ms) count=1 angle=18, step 2 angle=36 ... step 10 angle=180. Each 2s increment is 18 degrees up to 180. Matches.
At step 10 count=10 angle=180; step 11 count=20-11=9 angle=162; step 12 count=8 angle=144 ... step 19 count=1 angle=18; step 20 wraps to 0 angle=0. Decreases by 18 each 2s from 180 to 0. Matches.
step uses millis()/2000%20, so after step 19 (angle 18) it wraps to step 0 (angle 0) then step 1 (18) again, repeating the triangle wave indefinitely. Matches.
All three outputs io_0, io_1, io_2 are assigned the same count*18 in one call, and loop writes all three servos in the same iteration. Simultaneous update every 2s. Matches.

The implementation does not divide the total (0-540) into 10 ranges of 54. Instead it uses count (0-10) directly as the number of lit LEDs, where count is the per-servo step, not total/54. For total=162 (count=3) it lights 3, but the mapping is count-based not total/54; e.g. total=54 (count=1) lights 1 LED which coincidentally equals 54/54=1, but total=108 (count=2) lights 2 = 108/54=2. However the code never computes total; it derives LED count from count directly. Since all servos equal, total=3*count*18=54*count, so count=total/54 exactly. Equivalent behavior holds.
count = total/54 since total=3*count*18=54*count. Segment i lit when count>i, so number lit = count = total/54. total=162 -> count=3 -> segments 0,1,2 lit = 3 LEDs. Matches example.

Segment 0 -> pin 5 (A1), segment 1 -> pin 6 (A2), ... segment 8 -> pin 13 (A9), segment 9 -> pin 44 (A10). Wiring maps A1..A10 to pins 5,6,7,8,9,10,11,12,13,44. Lighting proceeds from segment 0 upward, i.e., A1 to A10. Matches.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which zeroes state, then analogWrite on pins 2-10 with hw_value_io_* all initialized to 0, so all channels are 0 (off) at power-on. However loop() immediately runs on first iteration (hw_started false, elapsed 0) and ProgramPage1 with phaseIndex 0 sets io_0=255 (rgb1 red) and others, so within the first loop pass the LEDs turn on. The initialization requirement is that upon powering on all LEDs are off; setup does write 0 to all pins, satisfying the initial off state before loop runs. The first loop iteration occurs after setup, so the off state exists at reset. This is satisfied.
At phaseIndex 0: io_0=255 (rgb1 R pin2), io_1=0, io_2=0 → rgb1 red. io_3=0, io_4=0, io_5=255 (rgb2 B pin7) → rgb2 blue. io_6=0, io_7=255 (rgb3 G pin9), io_8=0 → rgb3 green. Matches first pattern.

accumulatedMs accumulates elapsed ms; when >=2000 it subtracts 2000 and advances phaseIndex from 0 to 1. So first pattern lasts 2000ms. The loop gates at 10ms minimum, so timing is approximately 2s. Satisfies.
At phaseIndex 1: io_0=0, io_1=255 (rgb1 G pin3) → rgb1 green. io_3=255 (rgb2 R pin5), io_4=0, io_5=0 → rgb2 red. io_6=0, io_7=0, io_8=255 (rgb3 B pin10) → rgb3 blue. Matches second pattern.
When phaseIndex==1 and accumulatedMs>=2000, conditional_1=2, so phaseIndex becomes 2. Second pattern lasts 2000ms. Satisfies.

At phaseIndex 2 (else branches): io_0=0, io_1=0, io_2=255 (rgb1 B pin4) → rgb1 blue. io_3=0, io_4=255 (rgb2 G pin6), io_5=0 → rgb2 green. io_6=255 (rgb3 R pin8), io_7=0, io_8=0 → rgb3 red. Matches third pattern.
When phaseIndex==2 and accumulatedMs>=2000, the else branch sets conditional_1=0, so phaseIndex becomes 0. Third pattern lasts 2000ms. Satisfies.
After phaseIndex 2, transition sets phaseIndex back to 0, and the pattern logic re-evaluates each loop, so the sequence repeats indefinitely. Satisfies.
setup() writes hw_value_io_0/1/2 which are all false, so pins 2,3,4 are driven LOW at power-on/reset. Common-cathode RGB LED with all channels LOW is off.
phase = millis()/3000%4. For t in [0,3000) phase=0: io_0 = 0<3 true (red on), io_1 = false, io_2 = false. Pins 2 HIGH, 3 LOW, 4 LOW = red.
For t in [3000,6000) phase=1: io_0 true, io_1 true, io_2 false. Pins 2 HIGH, 3 HIGH, 4 LOW = red+green = yellow.
For t in [6000,9000) phase=2: io_0 true, io_1 true, io_2 true. Pins 2,3,4 all HIGH = red+green+blue = white.
For t in [9000,12000) phase=3: io_0 = 3<3 false, io_1 false, io_2 false. All pins LOW = off.
phase uses millis()/3000%4, so at t=12000 phase wraps to 0 and red resumes; loop() runs continuously re-evaluating phase, repeating indefinitely.

setup() writes hw_value_io_0=0 to the shift register (digits[0]=0x3f, inverted for common-anode wiring) and attaches all three servos; hw_value_io_1/2/3 are 0, so each servo.write(0) is issued at startup. Display shows 0 and all servos at 0 degrees.
digit = (millis()/2000)%10, so the displayed digit changes every 2000 ms; the loop recomputes and writes the digit each pass. Each number is displayed for 2 seconds.
For digit 0-2, base=digit/3*45=0, moving true (tick!=0 && digit!=9), so io_1=0, io_2=45, io_3=90. Matches.
For digit 3-5, base=1*45=45, so io_1=45, io_2=90, io_3=135. Matches.
For digit 6-8, base=2*45=90, so io_1=90, io_2=135, io_3=180. Matches.
For digit 9, moving is false (digit!=9 fails), so io_1=io_2=io_3=0. All servos return to 0.
digit=tick%10 wraps from 9 to 0 after 2 s, and the loop writes the new digit and servo values, repeating the cycle.

All three servo.write calls are issued in the same loop pass with no sequencing or wait for completion; there is no per-servo completion gating. The requirement of sequential movement (each completing before next starts) is not implemented.

setup() initializes all ten output pins with digitalWrite using hw_value_io_3..io_12, which are static-initialized to false, so every pin is driven LOW (LEDs off) before loop() runs. ProgramPage1_Init also zeroes state. No LED is HIGH at startup.
io_0 is analogRead(A3) (pot1 SIG per wiring). first=(int)(io_0*9.0/1023.0) maps 0..1023 to 0..9, and first is used as the lower bound of the lit range. This satisfies pot1 setting the lower bound.
io_1 is analogRead(A4) (pot2 SIG). last=(int)(io_1*9.0/1023.0) maps to 0..9 and is used as the upper bound. Satisfies pot2 setting the upper bound.

io_2 is analogRead(A5) (pot3 SIG). count=(int)(io_2*(last-first+1)/1023.0) scales the span by the pot fraction, so pot3 sets the fill fraction of the active range. At io_2=1023 count equals the full span; at 0 count is 0. This implements fill percentage within the range.

When first<=last, LEDs are lit for indices i where first<=i<first+count, i.e. sequentially from first upward. Endpoints: with count=span (io_2=1023) all indices first..last inclusive are lit. This matches lower-to-upper sequential lighting based on fill.

When first>last, the code swaps them (line 47) so first becomes the smaller and last the larger, then lights from the smaller index upward. The requirement says when lower>upper, LEDs light from upper to lower — i.e. starting at the upper (smaller) index and proceeding to the lower (larger) index. After swap, lighting starts at the smaller index (the original upper) and proceeds upward to the larger (original lower), which matches the required direction.
loop() re-samples all three pots every 10ms and calls ProgramPage1 then digitalWrite for all ten pins each iteration, so the bar graph continuously reflects pot changes.
All hw_value_io_3_segment_* statics initialize to false, and setup() writes LOW to pins 2-11 via the ternary on each false value, so all LEDs are off at reset.

pot1 is read from A3 (wired to pot1 SIG) and mapped via first=(int)(io_0*3/1023); segments 0-2 use first>0,>1,>2, giving 0-3 sequential LEDs on pins 2-4 (bargraph A1-A3). At 1023 first=3, all three on; at 0 all off.
pot2 is read from A4 and mapped via second=(int)(io_1*3/1023); segments 3-5 use second>0,>1,>2 driving pins 5-7 (bargraph A4-A6), giving 0-3 sequential LEDs.
pot3 is read from A5 and mapped via third=(int)(io_2*4/1023); segments 6-9 use third>0,>1,>2,>3 driving pins 8-11 (bargraph A7-A10), giving 0-4 sequential LEDs. At 1023 third=4, all four on.
loop() re-reads all three analog inputs every 5ms and calls ProgramPage1 then digitalWrite for all ten segments each pass, so the display continuously reflects current pot values.

ProgramPage1_Init sets digit=0; setup calls hw_shift595_io_0(0) which writes digits[0]=0x3f inverted to 0xC0 via shiftOut, and digitalWrite(2, LOW) since hw_value_io_3 is false. Display shows 0, LED off.
On btn1 rising edge (io_1 true, prevBtn1 false) with digit<9, conditional_1 = digit+1 and digit updated; loop then writes new digit to display. Increment by 1 implemented.
When digit==9 and btn1 edge, conditional_1=0, digit set to 0, display updated. Wrap to 0 implemented.
On btn2 rising edge with digit>0, conditional_3 = digit-1, digit updated and displayed. Decrement by 1 implemented.
When digit==0 and btn2 edge, conditional_3=9, digit set to 9, display updated. Wrap to 9 implemented.
Parity computation: for even digit, division by 2 equals truncation so conditional_4=0, arithmetic_5=digit/2, value_1 = (digit == 2*(digit/2)) true; digitalWrite(2, HIGH) turns LED on.
For odd digit, digit/2 < trunc(digit/2) so conditional_4=1, arithmetic_5=(digit/2)-1, 2*arithmetic_5 != digit, value_1 false, LED LOW.

After ProgramPage1 updates digit and parity, loop immediately calls hw_shift595_io_0 when value changed and digitalWrite(2,...) each iteration, so display and LED update in same loop pass after a press.

Edge detection via prevBtn1/prevBtn2 suppresses held-button repeats, but there is no time-based debounce; a single mechanical press producing multiple LOW/HIGH transitions within the 5ms sampling window can register multiple counts. No debounce delay or filtering is implemented.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which sets servo angles and display value to 0, then writes hw_value_io_0 (0) to the shift registers producing digits[0]=0x3f for both units and tens, and writes servo commands 0 to both servos. So displays show 00 and both servos at 0 degrees at power-on.
io_1 = analogRead(A3) (pot1). ProgramPage1 maps io_1 in [0,1023] to floor(io_1*99/1023) giving 0..99, and assigns to servo1 angle; loop writes it to servo on pin 2.
io_2 = analogRead(A4) (pot2). ProgramPage1 maps io_2 in [0,1023] to floor(io_2*99/1023) giving 0..99, assigned to servo2 angle; loop writes it to servo on pin 3.

hw_shift595_io_0 shifts units digit (value/1%10) first then tens digit (value/10%10) second; with two cascaded 595s the second shifted byte lands in sr1 (sevseg1) and first in sr2 (sevseg2), so tens on sevseg1 and units on sevseg2.
loop() runs every >=5ms, re-reads both pots, recomputes angles, and writes new servo commands when changed, so servos track pot values continuously.
Each loop iteration recomputes display value from servo1 angle and writes to shift registers when changed, so displays update in real-time with pot1.

setup() calls hw_shift595_io_0(0) since hw_value_io_0=0 differs from INT32_MIN. For value 0: first block segments=digits[0]=0x3f, bits=~0x3f=0xC0 sent to sr1 (sevseg1). Second block: valid && (value>=10) is false, so segments=0, bits=~0=0xFF sent to sr2 (sevseg2). digits[0]=0x3f is the '0' pattern; inverted 0xFF means all segments off. So sevseg1 gets 0xC0 (all segments off, extinguished) and sevseg2 gets 0xFF (all off). Wait—sevseg2 should show '0'. The second block sends 0xFF (all segments off) to sevseg2, not the '0' pattern. This contradicts the requirement that sevseg2 shows '0'.

loop() gates on hw_elapsed < 5UL, so it updates every 5ms, not every 1000ms. ProgramPage1 computes (millis()/1000*6)%100, which does increment by 6 per real second, but the display is refreshed every 5ms and the value only changes when millis()/1000 changes. The increment-by-6-per-second behavior is present via the formula. However the update cadence is 5ms not 1s; the value still changes by 6 each real second. The requirement is that every real second the timer increments by 6 and display updates. The formula yields that. But the 5ms gate means it recomputes frequently; the displayed value still steps by 6 each second. This satisfies the increment-by-6 requirement.
ProgramPage1 applies %100UL, so the value is always 0-99, and hw_shift595_io_0 only displays value%10 and (value/10)%10. Only last two digits are shown.

At 102 seconds, (102*6)%100 = 612%100 = 12, so displays show '12', not '2'. The requirement example says 102 should show '2'. The modulo is applied to the 6x-scaled value, not to the raw seconds. 102 seconds -> 612 -> %100 = 12. Displays '12'. Contradicts example.
loop() runs continuously; each 5ms it recomputes and updates display when value changes. The timer continues incrementing every second via millis()/1000*6. Continuous operation is implemented.
setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which resets state, then attaches servo and writes hw_value_io_0 which is initialized to 0.0, so the servo is commanded to 0° at startup.
ProgramPage1 computes step=millis()/2000%36 and angle=(step<=18?step:36-step)*10. For step 0..18 angle goes 0,10,...,180, each held 2000ms, matching upward sweep in 10° increments with 2s holds.
For step 19..35 the expression 36-step yields 17,16,...,1, so angle descends 170,160,...,10, then step 0 of next cycle gives 0. Decrements of 10° with 2s holds are produced, reaching 0.

setup() calls hw_shift595_io_0(0) which writes digit 0 (0x3f) inverted to 0xC0 via shiftOut, and all bar graph pins 2-11 are written LOW since hw_value_io_1..10 are false. Display shows 0, bar graph unlit at start.
count = millis()/2000%10 increments every 2000ms; loop updates io_0 and bar graph pins each pass, so displayed value increments by 1 every 2 seconds.
Modulo 10 on millis()/2000 makes count wrap from 9 to 0 and continue indefinitely; the loop keeps recomputing each pass.
hw_shift595_io_0 selects digits[value] for 0-9 and shifts inverted segment bits out to the 74HC595 driving sevseg1, so the display shows the current numeric value.
io_1..io_10 are count>0..count>9, so exactly N of pins 2..11 (A1..A10) are HIGH for value N, lighting N LEDs in order from A1.
shiftOut uses A0 (DS), A2 (SHCP), and A1 (STCP) to drive the 74HC595 whose outputs Q0-Q6 connect to sevseg1 segments, so sr1 drives the display.
Bar graph pins 2-11 are configured as OUTPUT and written directly with digitalWrite in setup and loop, matching the direct GPIO wiring to bargraph1.

pot1 (A3) is read into io_1; ProgramPage1 computes floor(io_1*9/1023) via the conditional subtract, giving 0..9 for 0..1023. hw_shift595_io_0 validates 0<=value<10 and outputs the digit pattern through shiftOut on A0/A2 with latch A1, matching sr1 wiring (DS=A0, SHCP=A2, STCP=A1).
loop re-reads A3 every 5ms and recomputes the digit each pass; the shift register is rewritten whenever the value changes, so the display tracks pot1 continuously.
io_2 from A4 maps to sysml_value_1 = io_2*90/1023, giving 0..90 for 0..1023. Servo1 attached to pin 2 writes (int)value, so angle range 0..90 is produced.
sysml_value_2 = 90 + io_2*90/1023 gives 90..180 for pot2 0..1023; servo2 on pin 3 writes that value, satisfying 90..180.
Each loop pass recomputes servo angles from pot2 and writes only when the integer command changes; Servo::write drives gradual motion, so servos move smoothly as pot2 is adjusted.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which sets stepIndex=0, then attaches each servo and writes hw_value_io_0/1/2 which are static-initialized to 0.0, so all three servos are commanded to 0 degrees at startup.

At stepIndex=0, the three nested conditionals yield value_0=0, value_1=0, value_2=0, written to servos. remainingMs starts at 2000 and decrements by elapsed each loop, so the position holds ~2s before stepIndex advances.
At stepIndex=1, value_0=0, value_1=45, value_2=90, matching step 2, held for 2000ms.
At stepIndex=2, value_0=45, value_1=90, value_2=135, matching step 3, held 2000ms.
At stepIndex=3, value_0=90, value_1=135, value_2=180, matching step 4, held 2000ms.
At stepIndex=4, value_0=135, value_1=180, value_2=0, matching step 5, held 2000ms.
At stepIndex=5, the else branches yield value_0=180, value_1=0, value_2=45, matching step 6, held 2000ms.
When remainingMs<=0 and stepIndex==5, conditional_0=1, so stepIndex wraps to 1 (step 2), not 0, repeating from step 2 indefinitely.
Servo.write() commands target angles directly with no interpolation or gradual stepping; the code jumps between discrete angles, so movements are not smoothed.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which sets displayCount=0 and elapsedAccMs=0. hw_value_io_0 is 0, differs from INT32_MIN, so hw_shift595_io_0(0) writes digits[0]=0x3f for both units and tens, showing '00'. Servos: hw_value_io_1/2/3 are 0, isfinite and in [0,180], command 0 != previous -1, so write(0) on all three. All initialization obligations met.

loop accumulates elapsed ms into elapsedAccMs; when >=2000 subtracts 2000 and increments displayCount (unless >=99). The 5ms gate means loop runs at most every 5ms, but accumulated elapsed is real time, so increments occur every ~2000ms. Increment by 1 implemented.
When displayCount >= 99 and 2000ms elapses, conditional_0=0, so displayCount resets to 0. At 99 it resets to 0 (exceeds 99 means next would be 100, so reset to 0 is correct).
sysml_value_1 = displayCount * 1.8, passed to hw_value_io_1, written to servo1 via (int) cast. For N=10 gives 18.0 -> 18. Matches N*1.8.
sysml_value_2 = displayCount * 1.2, written to servo2. For N=10 gives 12.0 -> 12. Matches N*1.2.
sysml_value_3 = displayCount * 0.6, written to servo3. For N=10 gives 6.0 -> 6. Matches N*0.6.
After ProgramPage1 updates hw_value_io_0, loop checks if it differs from previous and calls hw_shift595_io_0 immediately in the same loop iteration, updating displays.
After ProgramPage1 updates servo values, loop immediately writes new commands to all three servos in the same iteration when command differs from previous.

hw_shift595_io_0 shifts units digit (value/1 %10) first then tens digit (value/10 %10). With two cascaded 595s, first shifted byte ends in sr2 (units display sevseg2), second in sr1 (tens display sevseg1). One display shows tens, other units.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init (zeroing angles) then writes RGB pins from hw_value_io_1..6 which are still 0, and attaches servos writing hw_value_io_7..9 which are still 0. The potentiometer is never read before these writes, so the initial color is always black and servos go to 0 regardless of the pot's initial value. The first loop iteration only occurs after setup completes.
For io_0 in [0,341], red = io_0*255/341, giving 0 at 0 and 255 at 341, monotonic increase. Matches requirement.
For io_0 in [342,682], green = (io_0-341)*255/341, giving 255/341≈0.75 at 342 and 255 at 682, increasing. Matches requirement.
For io_0 in [683,1023], blue = (io_0-682)*255/341, giving 255/341≈0.75 at 683 and 255 at 1023, increasing. Matches requirement.
rgb1 uses io_1..3 (value_0..2) and rgb2 uses io_4..6 (value_3..5), computed by identical formulas from the same io_0, so both LEDs always receive the same values.
Servo angle = io_0*180/1023, mapping 0→0 and 1023→180. Matches requirement.
Accumulators add elapsed ms each step and only update angle when >=2000, then subtract 2000. So each servo holds its angle for at least 2000ms between updates. Matches requirement.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which sets phaseIndex=0, but hw_value_io_* globals remain false/0. digitalWrite writes LOW to pins 2-10 (LEDs off). Servos attach and write 0 (hw_value_io_9/10/11=0, valid range, previous=-1 so write(0) executes). All LEDs off and all servos at 0° at power-on.

phaseIndex 0..6 map to color bits: phase0 R only (red), phase1 G (green), phase2 B (blue), phase3 R+G (yellow), phase4 G+B (cyan), phase5 R+B (magenta), phase6 R+G+B (white). Sequence matches red,green,blue,yellow,cyan,magenta,white.
phaseTimeMs increments by 10 each loop iteration (loop gated to 10ms). Transition when phaseTimeMs+10>=2000, i.e. at phaseTimeMs=1990, so each phase lasts 2000ms = 2 seconds.
phaseIndex 0 (red): servo1=0.0, servo2=45.0, servo3=90.0. Matches Red spec.
phaseIndex 1 (green): servo1=45.0, servo2=90.0, servo3=135.0. Matches Green spec.
phaseIndex 2 (blue): servo1=90.0, servo2=135.0, servo3=180.0. Matches Blue spec.
phaseIndex 3 (yellow): servo1=135.0, servo2=180.0, servo3=0.0. Matches Yellow spec.
phaseIndex 4 (cyan): servo1=180.0, servo2=0.0, servo3=45.0. Matches Cyan spec.
phaseIndex 5 (magenta): servo1=0.0, servo2=45.0, servo3=90.0. Matches Magenta spec.
phaseIndex 6 (white): servo1=90.0, servo2=135.0, servo3=180.0. Matches White spec.
When phaseIndex==6 and timer expires, conditional_0=0, wrapping back to phase 0; loop() runs continuously so the cycle repeats indefinitely.

setup() configures pins 2,3,4 as outputs for RGB and attaches servos on 5,6,7; ProgramPage1_Init sets colorIndex=0, and index 0 yields io_0=true (R on) with G/B false, so the sequence begins with Red.
At colorIndex 0, io_0=true (Red), io_3=0.0, io_4=90.0, io_5=180.0, matching servo1 0, servo2 90, servo3 180.
At colorIndex 1, io_1=true (Green), io_3=90.0, io_4=180.0, io_5=0.0, matching servo1 90, servo2 180, servo3 0.
At colorIndex 2, io_2=true (Blue), io_3=180.0, io_4=0.0, io_5=90.0, matching servo1 180, servo2 0, servo3 90.
At colorIndex 3, io_0=true and io_1=true (Red+Green=Yellow), io_3=45.0, io_4=135.0, io_5=180.0. Servo3 225 is unsupported so 180 is the allowed fallback.
At colorIndex 4, io_1=true and io_2=true (Green+Blue=Cyan), io_3=135.0, io_4=180.0 (225 unsupported fallback), io_5=45.0.
At colorIndex 5, io_0=true and io_2=true (Red+Blue=Magenta), io_3=180.0 (225 unsupported fallback), io_4=45.0, io_5=135.0.
At colorIndex 6, io_0=true, io_1=true, io_2=true (White), io_3=0.0, io_4=90.0, io_5=180.0, matching initial positions.
phaseMs increments by 10 per loop iteration gated by 10ms elapsed, and colorIndex advances only when phaseMs>=2000, so each color persists ~2000ms.
When colorIndex==6 and phaseMs>=2000, conditional_0 is set to 0, wrapping back to Red, so the sequence repeats continuously.

At reset, ProgramPage1_Init sets number=0, but setup() never calls ProgramPage1, so hw_value_io_1 stays 0 and hw_shift595_io_1(0) writes digit 0 to both displays (showing "00"). Bar graph pins 2-11 are written LOW (off). Servos: hw_value_io_3/4/5 are 0, and setup attaches and writes 0 to each servo. All initial conditions satisfied.
number = millis()/2000UL%100, so it increments by 1 every 2000ms. The loop runs every ~10ms and recomputes number from millis, so the displayed value increments each 2s.
The modulo 100 in millis()/2000UL%100 wraps number from 99 back to 0, satisfying reset when exceeding 99.
segment_0..9 are set to number/10>k, so exactly tens-digit count of bar graph LEDs (pins 2-11) are HIGH. For number 37, number/10=3, segments 0,1,2 true → 3 LEDs lit. Matches requirement.
io_3 = units*18, written to servo1 on pin 12. For units 0-9 gives 0-162 degrees, within 0-180. Matches requirement.

io_4 = units ? min(180, units*18+60) : 0. For units 0 gives 0 (not 60), and for units 7,8,9 the min clamps to 180 instead of 186/204/222. Requirement says units*18+60 unconditionally, so values differ for units=0 and units>=7.

io_5 = units ? min(180, units*18+120) : 0. For units 0 gives 0 (not 120), and for units>=4 the min clamps to 180 instead of 192/210/228/246/264. Requirement says units*18+120 unconditionally, so values differ.

loop recomputes number from millis each ~10ms and immediately writes displays, bar graph, and servos when values change. On each increment the new values are applied in the same loop iteration, so updates are immediate.

setup() initializes all hw_value_io_* to false and writes LOW to every output pin (8-13,44,45,2-7), so all bar graph LEDs and both RGB LEDs are off at reset. First loop() call at millis()<2000 gives tick=0, index=-1, all outputs false, so still off.
index cycles 0..7 mapping to io_0..io_7 which drive pins 8,9,10,11,12,13,44,45 = A1..A8. Only one io is true at a time (index==N comparisons), so one LED lit at a time in order A1 to A8.
tick=millis()/2000, index=(tick-1)%8. index 0 spans millis 2000-3999 (2s), index 1 spans 4000-5999, etc. Each LED lit for 2000ms.
index=(tick-1)%8 wraps from 7 back to 0, so after A8 (index 7) the next tick gives index 0 = A1.

For index 0-3, first=true. io_8 (pin2=rgb1:R) = first = HIGH, io_9 (pin3=rgb1:G)=second=false, io_10 (pin4=rgb1:B)=false → rgb1 red. io_11 (pin5=rgb2:R)=second=false, io_12 (pin6=rgb2:G)=second=false, io_13 (pin7=rgb2:B)=first=HIGH → rgb2 blue. Correct.

For index 4-7, second=true, first=false. io_8 (rgb1:R)=false, io_9 (rgb1:G)=second=true, io_10 (rgb1:B)=false → rgb1 green. io_11 (rgb2:R)=second=true, io_12 (rgb2:G)=second=true, io_13 (rgb2:B)=false → rgb2 yellow (red+green). Correct.
setup() initializes hw_value_io_1/2/3 to false (static zero-init) and writes LOW to pins 2,3,4 before any loop iteration, so all three cathode-driven channels are off at power-on/reset.
analogRead(A3) yields 0..1023; io_0<341 sets io_1 true, io_2/io_3 false, so pin2 HIGH (red on cathode LED) and pins 3,4 LOW. First third maps to red.
For 341<=io_0<682, sysml_value_1 true and others false; pin3 HIGH (green), pins 2,4 LOW. Second third maps to green.
For io_0>=682, sysml_value_2 true, others false; pin4 HIGH (blue), pins 2,3 LOW. Final third maps to blue.
loop() re-reads A3 every 10ms and recomputes ProgramPage1 then writes pins 2,3,4 each pass, so color tracks the potentiometer continuously.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which sets servo state vars to 0.0, but the servo write blocks in setup use hw_value_io_2/3/4 which are static-initialized to 0.0, so all three servos write 0. All segment statics are false, so digitalWrite(5..13,44) all write LOW. Servos at 0 and all segments off at startup.
io_0=analogRead(A3) (pot1). For io_0<=0 ->0; >=1023 ->180; else io_0*180/1023. This maps 0..1023 to 0..180 directly. Servo written via write((int)value). Matches direct control 0-180.
io_1=analogRead(A4) (pot2). Same mapping 0..1023 -> 0..180 with clamps at 0 and 180. Servo2 written from hw_value_io_3. Matches direct control.

servo3 uses average of io_0,io_1 rounded via +0.5 then int cast (with a correction term for the fractional part). Both >=1023 ->180, both <=0 ->0, else rounded_avg*180/1023. This is average rounded to nearest integer scaled to 0-180. Matches.

Each segment k (0..9) is lit when rounded_avg*10/1023 >= k+1. At avg=0 all thresholds >=1 fail -> all off. At avg=1023, 1023*10/1023=10 >=10 -> all on. Segments lit in order from segment_0 (pin5/A1) to segment_9 (pin44/A10). Matches 0-10 scaling with ordered lighting.

D2 is read with pullup and inverted (LOW=press), debounced, and passed as io_0. On a rising edge of io_0 (press), mode=(mode+1)%3 cycles 0->1->2->0, matching off/on/breath. The edge detection uses prevMode updated each call, so each press advances exactly one mode.

D3 press (io_1 rising edge) adjusts brightness in mode 1 (brightness+16, wrapping 240->16) and period in mode 2 (period-500 down to 500 then back to 2000). In mode 0 nothing changes, which is acceptable since off mode has no parameter. This adjusts the current mode's parameter.
io_3 is set to mode each call and written to TM1637 on D4/D5 via showNumberDec when changed. The display shows the mode number (0/1/2), satisfying 'mode number or parameter value'.
In mode 0, io_2 is set to 0, and analogWrite(9,0) keeps D9 off. Mode 0 is the initial state and reachable via D2 cycling.
In mode 1, io_2=brightness (initial 64, adjustable by D3 between 16 and 240), so D9 stays lit at adjustable brightness.
In mode 2, phase=(now-started)%period, ramp is triangular 0..period/2, and io_2=ramp*510/period gives 0..255..0 breathing. D3 changes period (speed) and resets started.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which sets count=0 and accumulatedMs=0. hw_value_io_0 is 0, so hw_shift595_io_0(0) writes digits[0]=0x3f inverted for both digits, showing '00'. All segment bools are false so pins 2-11 are LOW (bargraph off). hw_value_io_2/io_3 are 0, so both servos write 0 degrees. All initial conditions satisfied.
loop accumulates elapsed ms into sysml_state_accumulatedMs and when >=2000 subtracts 2000 and increments count (unless >=99). The 10ms gate and elapsed accumulation produce a 2-second increment.

hw_shift595_io_0 shifts units digit (value/1%10) first then tens digit (value/10%10) second; with two cascaded 595s the second shifted byte lands in sr1 driving sevseg1 (tens) and first in sr2 driving sevseg2 (units). Tens on sevseg1, units on sevseg2.

The bar graph thresholds use (count*10.0)/99.0 compared to integers 1..10, so at count=50 the value is 5.05, lighting 5 LEDs; at count=99 it is 10.0 lighting 10. This is proportional (count/99*10) rather than count/10, but the example (50->5) holds and it is proportional to the number.

sysml_value_11 and sysml_value_12 compute (int32_t)(count*1.8) minus a floor-correction, yielding floor(count*1.8). For count=50 this is 90, count=99 gives 178. The wrapper writes these to both servos. Matches (number*1.8) degrees.

When count>=99 the increment branch sets conditional_0=0, so at count=99 the next 2s tick resets to 0. All outputs (displays, bar graph, servos) are recomputed from sysml_state_count each loop, so they update accordingly.

pot1 is read from A3 into hw_value_io_9, passed as io_9, and mapped via (io_9*255.0)/1023.0 into sysml_value_0/3/6, which drive analogWrite on pins 2, 5, 8 (rgb1:R, rgb2:R, rgb3:R). The mapping spans 0..255 for the 0..1023 ADC domain, satisfying the red component requirement for all three LEDs.

pot2 is read from A4 into hw_value_io_10, passed as io_10, mapped via (io_10*255.0)/1023.0 into sysml_value_1/4/7, driving analogWrite on pins 3, 6, 9 (rgb1:G, rgb2:G, rgb3:G). The 0..1023 to 0..255 mapping satisfies the green component requirement.
The blue outputs sysml_value_2/5/8 are hardcoded false, and the corresponding pins 4, 7, 10 are driven with digitalWrite LOW (cathode common, so off). Blue is fixed at 0 for all three LEDs.

pot1 (io_9) is mapped via (io_9*180.0)/1023.0 into sysml_value_9, assigned to io_11, which drives servo1 on pin 11 through the range guard 0..180. The 0..1023 to 0..180 mapping satisfies the servo1 requirement.
pot2 (io_10) is mapped via (io_10*180.0)/1023.0 into sysml_value_10, assigned to io_12, which drives servo2 on pin 12 through the 0..180 guard. Satisfies the servo2 requirement.

io_13 is overwritten with millis()/2000%2 ? 180 : 0, independent of the pots, and drives servo3 on pin 13. At t=0..1999 it is 0, at 2000..3999 it is 180, alternating every 2 seconds. Satisfies the requirement.
The loop gates on hw_elapsed < 10UL, so updates occur every ~10 ms, not every 100 ms. The requirement explicitly states 100 ms; the implemented period is 10 ms, a concrete mismatch.
setup() initializes hw_value_io_2..7 to 0 and writes analogWrite 0 to pins 2-7 before any loop iteration, so both RGB LEDs start off.
pot1 on A3 is read into io_0 and ProgramPage1 computes position=adc*6/1023, i.e. hue sector 0..6 (0..360 degrees) for rgb1.
pot2 on A4 is read into io_1 and the same loop maps it to position 0..6 (0..360 degrees) for rgb2.
The sector/peak/ramp computation is a standard HSV-to-RGB conversion with hue from position, producing per-channel RGB values.
Peak channel is set to 255 and the ramp channel scales 0..255, with the third channel 0, which corresponds to S=1, V=1.
Computed io_2..io_4 drive pins 2,3,4 (rgb1) and io_5..io_7 drive pins 5,6,7 (rgb2) via analogWrite.
loop() re-reads both pots every 5 ms and recomputes/writes all six channels, so colors update continuously.
Hue is quantized to 1024 ADC steps over 360 degrees and the ramp channel is linear in fraction, giving gradual per-step changes; no abrupt jumps beyond the discrete ADC resolution.
