loop() samples HC-SR04 on D8/D9, converts pulse to cm (pulse/58.0), passes it to ProgramPage1 which stores the truncated integer in sysml_state_displayedDistanceIntCm and outputs it via io_3; loop() then calls showNumberDec on the TM1637 (D4/D5) with that value, so measured distance is displayed.

When a valid echo is measured (io_2 true) and io_1 < 10.0, sysml_lazy_2 becomes true and is written to *io_0; loop() then drives D13 HIGH. For io_1 >= 10.0 or invalid measurement, io_0 is false and D13 is LOW, so the <10cm threshold is implemented.

When analogRead(A0) returns >700, ProgramPage1 sets io_1=255.0 and io_2=1000. loop() writes analogWrite(9,255) which is full brightness, and since 1000 is within [31,65535] and differs from initial hw_tone_io_2=-1, tone(6,1000) is called, sounding the buzzer. Both outputs match the requirement.

DHT11 is constructed on pin 7 (line 62) and read via hw_dht_0.read()/readTemperature() (lines 80-81). The loop gates on hw_elapsed < 5UL returning early (line 75), so ProgramPage1 is only invoked after ~5ms steps; accumulatedMs accumulates elapsed and triggers serial output when >= 5000 (line 42), i.e. every 5 seconds. On trigger, Serial.print("Temperature") and Serial.println(value) output the temperature (line 94). The DHT is sampled at most every 2000ms (line 78), which is within the 5s period, and the last valid temp is latched. The path from D7 DHT11 read to serial output every 5s is implemented.
ProgramPage1_Init sets ledIndex=7; colors[7]=7 gives all channels 0, and setup writes analogWrite 0 to pins 3,4,5 before any loop call, so the LED starts off.

Debounce requires 150ms stable, then ProgramPage1 sees rising edge, increments index from 7 to 0, colors[0]=0 -> R=0,G=0,B=0. Wait: colors[0]=0 means all off, not Red. The first press yields Off, not Red.
From Red state index would be 1 (colors[1]=1 -> R only). Next press increments to index 2, colors[2]=2 -> G only, which is Green. So Red->Green holds.
Green is index 2 (colors[2]=2). Next press index 3, colors[3]=4 -> B only, Blue. Correct.
Blue is index 3 (colors[3]=4). Next press index 4, colors[4]=3 -> R+G = Yellow. Correct.
Yellow is index 4 (colors[4]=3). Next press index 5, colors[5]=6 -> G+B = Cyan. Correct.
Cyan is index 5 (colors[5]=6). Next press index 6, colors[6]=5 -> R+B = Magenta. Correct.
Magenta is index 6 (colors[6]=5). Next press index 7, colors[7]=7 -> R+G+B = White. Correct.
White is index 7 (colors[7]=7). Next press index 0, colors[0]=0 -> all off. Correct.
Off is index 0 (colors[0]=0). Next press index 1, colors[1]=1 -> R only = Red. Cycle repeats. Correct.
manual_debounce_input only sets stable after 150ms of unchanged raw; a shorter press never updates stable, so io_0 stays false and no edge is seen. State unchanged.

The 2000ms gate only applies to the first press (started false). After started=true, subsequent presses increment index immediately regardless of elapsed time, so color states can last far less than 2 seconds.

loop samples D2 into hw_value_io_0 and calls ProgramPage1; when io_0 is HIGH and previousPressed is false, count increments by 1 and previousPressed is set to io_0, so a press edge increments the count once.

After ProgramPage1 updates hw_value_io_1 from sysml_state_count, loop compares it to hw_display_previous_io_1 and calls showNumberDec with the new count when changed, so the TM1637 displays the current count.
For odd count, sysml_value_1 = count != 2*floor(count/2) evaluates true; loop writes HIGH to D13 when hw_value_io_2 is true, lighting the LED.
For even count, sysml_value_1 = count != 2*(count/2) evaluates false; loop writes LOW to D13, turning the LED off.

D2 is read as active-low (digitalRead(2)==LOW) into io_0; ProgramPage1 toggles sysml_state_distanceMode on the rising edge of the press (io_0 true and previousPressed false), then sets previousPressed=io_0. In distance mode io_4 (ultrasonic valid) gates selectedValue from io_3 (distance); otherwise io_2 (DHT valid) gates selectedValue from io_1 (temperature). The toggled value is written to the TM1637 display, so pressing the button switches between temperature and distance display.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which sets counterValue=0, but the actual displayed value comes from ProgramPage1's static 'number' (initialized 0) and hw_value_io_4=0. setup() calls hw_shift595_io_4(0) which shifts digits[0]=0x3f for both digits, displaying '00'.
btn1 on pin2 sets io_0 true; direction=1. On rising edge direction!=previous triggers number=(number+1+100)%100, incrementing by 1. Display updates via hw_shift595_io_4 when value changes.
btn2 on pin3 sets io_1 true; direction=-1. number=(number-1+100)%100 decrements by 1 (with wrap). Display updates.
btn3 on pin4 sets io_2 true; number=0 and direction=0, so display resets to 0.
interval=100+(io_3*900/1023) where io_3 is analogRead 0..1023, giving 100ms..1000ms. Repeat stepping occurs when held (direction==previous and elapsed>=interval). Matches 0.1s to 1s range.
After ProgramPage1 updates hw_value_io_4, loop compares to previous and calls hw_shift595_io_4 immediately, updating the display in the same iteration.
number=(number+direction+100)%100 wraps 99+1 to 0.
number=(number+direction+100)%100 wraps 0-1 to 99.
setup() calls pinMode(2..9, OUTPUT) for all eight pins, satisfying the requirement to set pins 2 through 9 as outputs at power-up.

Wiring maps A->2, B->3, C->4, D->5, E->6, F->7, G->8, DP->9. For common anode, segments are lit by LOW. Digit 5 needs A,C,D,F,G lit (LOW) and B,E off (HIGH). setup writes pin2(A)=LOW, pin3(B)=HIGH, pin4(C)=LOW, pin5(D)=LOW, pin6(E)=HIGH, pin7(F)=LOW, pin8(G)=LOW, pin9(DP)=HIGH, which lights A,C,D,F,G and blanks B,E,DP — displaying 5.
ProgramPage1_Init sets all intensities to 0; setup writes analogWrite 0 to pins 5-7 and LOW to bar graph pins 8-13,44,45, so RGB and bar graph are off at start.
On rising edge of btn1 with red<255, red becomes red+32 when <=223, else 255. From 0→32, 32→64, ..., 192→224, 224→255. All increments are 32 within range.
When redIntensity>=255 (i.e., 255), the branch sets conditional_1=0, so next press resets to 0.
Green uses identical logic: rising edge with green<255 adds 32 (or clamps to 255 when >223).
When greenIntensity>=255, conditional_3=0, resetting green to 0 on next press.
Blue uses identical logic: rising edge with blue<255 adds 32 (or clamps to 255 when >223).
When blueIntensity>=255, conditional_5=0, resetting blue to 0 on next press.

segments = latest/32 (or 8 if 255), and segment_i = segments>i. For 32→1, 64→2, ..., 224→7, 255→8. selectedColor is set to the pressed button's color before output, so bar graph reflects the adjusted color.
io_3/io_4/io_5 are set from red/green/blue intensities and written via analogWrite to pins 5/6/7 (R/G/B), producing combined color.
manual_debounce_input requires raw stable for 25ms before updating stable state; buttons sampled through this function.

On receiving BUZZ, hw_rx_parse sets value=1 and returns true, so io_1_valid is true; ProgramPage1 sets began=millis() and active=true, outputting 1000. The tone command 1000 is within [31,65535], so tone(6,1000) starts the buzzer on D6. After 500ms, active becomes false, output 0, and noTone(6) stops it. The 500ms duration and D6 pin are implemented.

loop() computes hw_elapsed from millis() deltas, passes it as io_2; ProgramPage1 accumulates it and increments displayValue when accumulatedMs>=1000, then writes to TM1637 via showNumberDec on change. Each ~1000ms of elapsed time increments the displayed value, satisfying per-second increment.

On D2 HIGH with previousPressed false, accumulatedMs and displayValue are reset to 0, then io_1=0 is written; loop detects change from previous display value and calls showNumberDec(0), clearing the display.

setup() configures A0 as INPUT, D9 as OUTPUT, and constructs TM1637Display on pins 4/5 with setBrightness(7,true) before any display write, so the system enters a displayable and brightness-controllable state. The initial analogWrite(9,0) and showNumberDec(0) are harmless; loop() then drives both.

loop() samples analogRead(A0) into hw_value_io_0 every 5 ms and calls analogWrite(9, (int)(hw_value_io_0*255.0/1023.0)). For A0=0 output is 0; for A0=1023 output is 255; intermediate values scale linearly, so D9 brightness tracks the potentiometer.

ProgramPage1 computes io_2=(int32_t)(io_0*255.0/1023.0), the same scaled brightness value, and loop() writes it to the TM1637 via showNumberDec when it changes. A0=0 shows 0, A0=1023 shows 255, so the displayed number corresponds to the brightness control.
setup() calls pinMode(8, OUTPUT) for the buzzer pin on pin 8, matching the wiring.
setup() calls Wire.begin() then hw_bus_0.begin() storing the result in hw_bus_0_ready, which gates RTC reads.
loop() periodically (every 10ms) reads hw_bus_0.now().unixtime() into hw_value_io_0 when ready, so time is continuously sampled.
ProgramPage1 sets io_2=1000 when io_1 valid and io_0>=1732423740 (2024-11-24T04:49:00 UTC); loop then calls tone(8,1000) since 1000 is in [31,65535].
Before threshold, io_0<1732423740 makes sysml_conditional_1=0, so hw_value_io_2=0, command=0, and noTone(8) is called (initial hw_tone_io_2=-1 differs from 0 so noTone executes).

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which sets evenOn=true, then writes hw_value_io_0_segment_* initializers: segment_0,2,4,6,8 = true (HIGH) and segment_1,3,5,7,9 = false (LOW). Pins 2,4,6,8,10 drive bargraph A1,A3,A5,A7,A9 (odd positions) HIGH, and pins 3,5,7,9,11 drive A2,A4,A6,A8,A10 (even positions) LOW. So even positions are off and odd positions are on at power-on, contradicting the requirement.

After 2s the accumulator reaches >=2000 and toggles evenOn to false. ProgramPage1 then sets segment_0,2,4,6,8 = evenOn = false and segment_1,3,5,7,9 = !evenOn = true. Pins 2,4,6,8,10 (odd positions) go LOW and pins 3,5,7,9,11 (even positions) go HIGH. This is the opposite of the required transition (even off, odd on): odd positions turn off and even positions turn on.

The accumulator subtracts 2000 and toggles evenOn each time it reaches 2000, so alternation continues indefinitely every ~2s. However the mapping is inverted: evenOn=true lights odd bargraph positions and evenOn=false lights even positions, so the alternation is between the wrong sets relative to the requirement. The sequence does alternate every 2s but with swapped even/odd assignment.
setup() calls Serial.begin(9600) unconditionally at power-up, establishing serial communication.

hw_bus_0_ready is set from hw_bus_0.begin(104,&Wire); on the first loop, sample_valid from getEvent sets io_3 true, ProgramPage1 sets readyPulse/readySent, and io_4 triggers Serial.println("MPU6050 ready!"). The message is printed only after a successful getEvent, which is the successful-init path.
Each loop iteration (gated to 5ms) calls hw_bus_0.getEvent and stores acceleration.x/y/z into io_0..io_2, which are passed to ProgramPage1 and forwarded to serial values.
When reportPulse triggers, the code prints X, Y, Z with 2 decimals and " m/s^2". Adafruit getEvent returns acceleration in m/s^2, matching the required units and format.

The delay is implemented via the accumulator: after a report, waitingForDelay is set and delayStartPending resets the accumulator; subsequent iterations add hw_elapsed until >=500, then the next report occurs. This yields a 500ms interval between loop reports, satisfying the 500ms delay per loop.
setup() calls pinMode(2..9, OUTPUT) for all eight pins 2 through 9, satisfying the requirement at power-up.
loop() calls hw_rx_poll every iteration (after the 5ms gate), which loops on Serial.available()>0 and reads bytes, so serial availability is continuously checked.

For common anode, a segment is lit by driving its pin LOW. patterns[] are active-high bitmaps (e.g. digit 0 = 0x3f lights A-F). ProgramPage1 sets io bits from pattern bits, and loop writes LOW when bit is true, HIGH when false. So digit 0 (0x3f) drives pins 2-7 LOW (A-F lit) and pin 8 HIGH (G off), pin 9 HIGH (DP off) — correct common-anode rendering.

hw_rx_parse accepts only 0-9, sets digit, and the same digit drives the segment outputs; the displayed digit equals the parsed serial value. Non-digit input is rejected and display retains prior digit, which is consistent with showing the serial input value.

Pulse0 accumulates elapsed ms; when phase reaches 3000 it wraps and started becomes true, then value is true while phase<100, producing io_1=1000 (tone on D6) for ~100ms each 3s. However the first pulse requires phase to reach 3000, and phase only advances when enabled (run value true). Trace: initial phase 0, enabled false first call, then enabled true; each loop adds elapsed. When phase crosses 3000, started=true and phase wraps to remainder. The tone output is 1000 for phase<100, i.e., ~100ms beep every 3s. This satisfies periodic beep on D6.

Button edge detection toggles sysml_state_paused on rising edge (io_0 true and previousPressed false). When paused, sysml_conditional_5=0 so io_1=0, noTone(6) called, stopping beep. This pauses periodic beeping.

Pressing button again while paused toggles sysml_state_paused back to false; then io_1 follows pulse value, and tone resumes when pulse value true. However note: while paused, enabled remains run value true, so phase continues advancing; on resume the beep resumes at current phase. This restores periodic beeping.
setup() calls Serial.begin(9600), initializing serial communication at power-up.
setup() calls pinMode(4, INPUT), configuring the button pin (pin 4 per wiring) as INPUT.
loop() reads digitalRead(4) each iteration, debounces it, and ProgramPage1 records began=millis() on press and computes elapsed duration on release, so press duration is measured continuously.
On release trigger, loop prints "Button pressed duration: " then the value in seconds (ms/1000.0) then "s", matching the required format.

evidence.text: if (hw_value_serial_0_trigger) { Serial.print("Button pressed duration: "); Serial.print(hw_value_serial_0_value_0); Serial.println("s"); }

items.reason: The loop uses a 5ms step gate (hw_elapsed < 5UL return) and the debounce helper requires 25ms stability, providing short delays for bounce handling.

setup() calls pinMode(3, INPUT_PULLUP) and pinMode(9, OUTPUT). Pin 3 is the button (wired to 5V via resistor, GND when pressed) and pin 9 is the buzzer. INPUT_PULLUP is an input mode, satisfying the requirement; buzzer pin is OUTPUT.
loop() reads digitalRead(3) each iteration (throttled to 5ms), storing the pressed state into hw_value_io_0, which is passed to ProgramPage1. This continuously samples the button.

When pressed, digitalRead(3)==LOW so io_0 is true; ProgramPage1 sets io_1=262. The tone command 262 is within [31,65535], differs from hw_tone_io_1 (-1 initially), so tone(9,262) is called, producing 262Hz on the buzzer pin.
When not pressed, digitalRead(3)==HIGH so io_0 is false; ProgramPage1 sets io_1=0. The tone command becomes 0, differing from previous 262, so noTone(9) is called, silencing the buzzer.
setup() calls Serial.begin(9600), initializing serial communication at power-up.
setup() calls pinMode(4, INPUT), and the circuit connects the button to Arduino pin 4, matching the specified pin.
loop() re-samples digitalRead(4) every 5ms and passes the value into ProgramPage1, so the button is continuously checked.
When io_0 is HIGH, serial_0_trigger = report && io_0 is true (report true on first call or change), and loop prints "Button pressed".
When io_0 is LOW, serial_1_trigger = report && !io_0 is true, and loop prints "Button not pressed".
setup() calls Serial.begin(9600), initializing serial communication at power-up.
setup() calls pinMode(4, INPUT), configuring the button pin as INPUT.
loop() repeatedly reads digitalRead(4) (throttled to 5ms) and passes the value to ProgramPage1, so the button is continuously checked.
digitalRead LOW maps to hw_value_io_0=true; ProgramPage1 sets trigger on change and the print selects "Button pressed" when value is true, i.e. when pin is LOW.
When pin is HIGH, digitalRead==LOW is false, so value false and the ternary prints "Button not pressed"; trigger fires on change and initial report.
Circuit connects push button to Arduino pin 4; code uses pinMode(4,...) and digitalRead(4), matching the diagram.

setup initializes Serial and pins A0/D2; loop samples analogRead(A0) and digitalRead(2), passes them to ProgramPage1 which forwards io_0 and io_1 to serial_0_value_0/1, and when the 1000ms accumulator threshold fires, both Serial.print lines emit the A0 value and D2 state. The accumulator adds elapsed ms each iteration and subtracts 1000 on trigger, so output occurs once per ~1s cycle. Both required values are printed on the trigger.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init setting count=0, then writes hw_value_io_3..8 (all 0) to pins 5-10 via analogWrite, so RGB LEDs are off. hw_value_io_9 is 0, and hw_shift595_io_9(0) writes digits[0]=0x3f inverted to 0xC0, which with the wiring (Q0..Q6 to A..G, common cathode via MR=VCC) lights segments for '0'. Display shows 0, LEDs off.

Each button's rising edge (io true and prev false) increments count by 1 (or resets to 0 at >=15), and loop writes the new count to the display via hw_shift595_io_9 and updates RGB. Count is displayed.
io_9 is set to n%10, so for counts 10-15 the display shows the ones digit (0-5).
When count>=15 and a button edge occurs, count is set to 0. At count 0, io_3..io_8 evaluate to 0 (n>0 false), so all RGB channels are off, matching initial state.
For count<5 (and >0), io_3=255 (red on pin5), io_5=255 (blue on pin7), io_4=io_6=io_7=io_8=0. rgb1 red, rgb2 blue. At count 0 all off (initial state, per R001).
For 5<=n<=9: io_4=255 (green pin6), io_6=255 (red pin8), io_7=255 (green pin9), io_3=io_5=io_8=0. rgb1 green, rgb2 red+green=yellow.
For n>=10: io_3=255 (red pin5), io_5=255 (blue pin7) => rgb1 purple; io_6=0, io_7=255 (green pin9), io_8=255 (blue pin10) => rgb2 cyan.
loop runs every >=5ms, samples buttons, calls ProgramPage1, then immediately writes analogWrite to all RGB pins and shift register for display. Updates occur in same loop iteration after press.
manual_debounce_input requires raw stable for >=25ms before updating stable state, and edge detection uses the debounced value, preventing false triggers.
setup() calls pinMode(2, OUTPUT) directly, configuring the buzzer pin as an output at power-up.

setup() computes hw_tone_command_io_0=262 (in 31..65535), differs from initial hw_tone_io_0=-1, so tone(2,262) is called. In loop, ProgramPage1 sets hw_value_io_0=262, command stays 262, equal to hw_tone_io_0 so no re-call, but tone continues running continuously at 262Hz on pin 2.

loop() samples A0 into hw_value_io_0 and passes it to ProgramPage1, which computes period = 200 + io_0*1800/1023 ms (200..2000 ms for ADC 0..1023) and toggles via millis()%period < period/2; the result is written to D13. The full 0.2–2 s range is reachable and the LED blinks at that period.
setup() calls Serial.begin(9600), initializing the serial monitor at power-up.
A DHT object is constructed on pin 2 as DHT22 and hw_dht_0.begin() is called in setup().
loop() periodically (every 2000ms) calls hw_dht_0.read() and readHumidity(), storing the value in hw_value_io_0 for continuous reading.
When a valid reading occurs, io_1 is true, ProgramPage1 sets trigger and cached humidity, and loop prints "Humidity: " followed by the value via Serial.println, matching the required format.
setup() calls Serial.begin(9600), matching the required baud rate at power-up.
setup() calls hw_servo_io_0.attach(9), attaching the servo object to pin 9.
setup() configures pin 3 with INPUT_PULLUP, which sets the pin mode to INPUT (with pull-up enabled). The button is on pin 3 per wiring, so the mode is set as INPUT.
loop() calls ProgramPage1 which sets serial_0_trigger=true and serial_0_value_0=servoAngle; then Serial.print/println outputs the angle each iteration.
loop() reads digitalRead(3) into hw_value_io_1 and passes it to ProgramPage1 as io_1, continuously sampling every 5ms.
When button pressed, digitalRead(3)==LOW yields io_1=true, ProgramPage1 sets servoAngle=180.0, and loop writes 180 to the servo.
When button not pressed, io_1=false, ProgramPage1 sets servoAngle=90.0, and loop writes 90 to the servo.
setup() calls Serial.begin(9600) at line 159, initializing serial communication at power-up.
setup() calls hw_bus_0.begin() and stores the result in hw_bus_0_ready, checking whether the RTC module can begin.
setup() reads hw_bus_0.now().unixtime() once and stores it in hw_value_io_0, which is the current time read once at power-up.
loop() calls hw_rx_poll each iteration, which reads Serial bytes into hw_rx_buffer and parses ISO datetime via hw_rx_parse, continuously reading serial input.

When a valid target is parsed, ProgramPage1 computes (io_2-io_0)/86400 with floor adjustment into reportedDays, and loop prints "D-" followed by the value. The day difference is computed and printed in the required format.
The RTC now() call appears only in setup() at line 163; loop() never calls hw_bus_0.now(), so current time is read only once.
setup() calls pinMode(2..6, OUTPUT) for all five pins, matching the wiring where LED1-5 anodes connect through resistors to pins 2-6.

loop() polls Serial each iteration via hw_rx_poll, which reads bytes, parses on newline or 20ms idle, and hw_rx_parse rejects values outside 0..31 (parsed<0 || parsed>31 returns false). Accepted values set hw_value_io_0_valid and update the stored value.

ProgramPage1 stores the accepted value and computes io_1..io_5 from bits 0..4; loop writes io_1 to pin2 (LED1) through io_5 to pin6 (LED5), so LED1 is LSB and LED5 is MSB. E.g. input 1 lights pin2 only, input 16 lights pin6 only.
setup() calls pinMode(2..13, OUTPUT) for all twelve pins 2 through 13, satisfying the requirement.

At millis()<1000, digit=0, previous=-1 so it proceeds. patterns[0]=0x06 sets segments B,C active (LOW) and others HIGH, then digitalWrite(10+0,HIGH) drives DIG1 high. Common anode with COM at 5V: DIG1 high means digit1 is off (anode not pulled low), so digit1 does not display 1. Also the segment pattern 0x06 is for common-cathode '1' (B,C on), but with active-low segments the lit segments are B,C which is correct for '1' only if the digit is enabled. Since DIG1 is driven HIGH (disabled), digit1 shows nothing.

Common-anode display: segment is lit when its pin is LOW. The model computes active-low segment masks (value true => LOW via ternary) and loop writes them to pins 2-9. That lights A,D,E,F,G = segments for '1'? Standard '1' is B,C. Here A,D,E,F,G lit and B,C off — that is the complement, i.e. it displays the inverse of '1'. So the segment pattern is wrong for common anode. This is a concrete violation.

For elapsed 1-2s, sysml_value_0==1. The computed segment booleans produce A,D,E,F,G lit and B,C off (see R002), which is not the digit '1' on a common-anode display; the pattern is inverted. So digit 1 is not correctly displayed.

Lit: C,E,F. Digit '2' needs A,B,D,E,G lit. Wrong pattern.

For value_0==3: value_2(A)=(3!=1)&&(3!=4)=true off; value_3(B)=(3!=5)&&(3!=6)=true off; value_4(C)=(3!=2)=true off; value_5(D)=(3!=1)&&(3!=4)&&(3!=7)=true off; value_6(E)=(3==0||3==2||3==6||3==8)=false lit; value_7(F)=(3==0||3==4||3==5||3==6||3==8||3==9)=false lit; value_8(G)=(3!=0)&&(3!=1)&&(3!=7)=true off.
